I bought the 3-pack of black v-neck CK's via Amazon in May'09.  I purchased men's size "Medium" based on the fact that I bought the same 3-pack last year in size "Large" and the fit was bigger than I wanted.  I am 5'10", 195lbs and usually wear a size "Large" in most men's tops.

In terms of sizing I was looking for a fit that is slightly snug versus too baggy (as the Larges were for me) so now that I have the size Mediums they are working out much better for my preference (especially since I've noticed they also tend to stretch out a bit over time).  Bad news is I have 6 of these tshirts clogging up my dresser drawers now, good news is since I have the Medium and Large sizes I can gain a few pounds and I'm still good to go (beer me).

I do agree with some other reviewers that CK tshirts do tend to be thin material and they aren't your typical stand alone t-shirt you can show off about town.  They are good tshirts under another piece of clothing, as pajama top, or working around the yard.  I actually like the fact that CK v-necks are thin because they are very comfortable to wear for incognito usage.

Style-wise a good looking t-shirt with nice looking v-neck shape.

Overall: 4 out of 5 stars. High marks for looks and comfort for my intended usage, minus 1 star for the slightly strange sizing causing inventory buildup in my dresser drawers.

These shirts are great V-Neck's that fit perfectly, are comfortable, and look great!

They can be used as a black under-shirt, if ever needed, but I love to wear these as every day shirts.  The nice cotton design is comfortable and washes great. After many washes I still find the shirt to be comfortable and fit the same way as always (the first wash/dry might make it - like all shirts - shrink a little).

These are some of my favorite shirts to wear, and I wear them all the time.

They fit as you would expect, I purchased medium (as I purchase medium shirts always) and it fit as it should.  At first it was a little too big, but after the first wash/dry it shaped properly and fits perfectly now.

The material is thick, and it doesn't' feel cheap at all, while it is nice and soft and great for sleeping in too (your significant other will love the softness of the material!).

When I purchased them, they were on sale and a great value - but even at regular price these shirts are definitely a great buy and can be worn as an every day shirt, as a black under shirt, or as a nice comfortable at home/night shirt.  I have recommend these (and the white versions, as undershirts) to my friends and purchase new ones every so often when I lose them, or people take them!

Lastly, they are made to last! I have had some of these for more than a year (coming up on almost two years, actually) and they still look great and fit perfectly -- after about a year I usually retire them to night shirts and get new fresh ones (as I tend to stain them here and there and wear them so much that I like to purchase fresh ones to wear out -- don't don't let that make you think they don't last, I could absolutely still wear them out if I wanted to!).

Update:

I'm about to place my 3rd order of these shirts. I ordered 9 over one year ago, and 9 one year prior to that. I am one of those guys who just sweats a lot. To ensure the shirts the world sees stay alive for longer, i wear these guys underneath. This product is outstanding and the price on Amazon can not be beat. Buxton owns the rights to the Dopp name and produces these "official Dopp" kits. The leather is good, feels solid and well stitched, but you can also get them in a slightly less expensive PVC leatherette version. You can also find these in some stores although the ones I found were double in price. Sometimes the bottoms are leather and sometimes the bottoms were a beaded plastic. Frankly I made sure to get the beaded plastic as it will last longer than a leather bottom. The key features if this Dopp kit are: 1) Construction feels solid. (Although the tag says made in China...you would feel better if it had a proud to be made in the USA tag...however, I don't think this is an issue here.) The leather and stitching feels strong. The zipper is a hefty enough piece of metal that will last. The leather handle is small enough that it fits under the fold of the kit's side if you do not want to use it. The inside is a traditional liner with a single razor pouch, however, the liner and pouch feel like they are made of a newer composite plastic material than the older plastic liners these type of kits used to have. The liner feels stronger and I doubt it will rip, which often happened with travel kits. 2) It has Dopp stamped on it, on two flaps/tabs. The tabs are aesthetic choices but look good and remind you that you have a "real" Dopp and not some random "Men's Toiletry Bag."  There are newer types of "Dopp" kit's out there made out of nylon mesh. If you like that I would recommend something by L.L. Bean or Swiss Army. But for something more traditional I would only recommend this brand right here...

They are quite comfortable, but do require some breaking-in. I wore them around the house for about a week before wearing them outside. They ARE stiff, but it is important to remember that wingtips are SUPPOSED to be stiff. The toe-cap and wings (longwings on these shoes) are there to make the shoe sturdier than standard oxfords. I had three pairs of these that fit perfectly when I first got them, but after several months I noticed my ankles were drafty.  I got out the measuring tape and my nominally 30" inseams (which started out closer to 31") now measured just 28".  This happened to all 3 pairs after maybe 15 laundry cycles.  I wash and dry them in compliance with the laundry label, and they do just fine, but they apparently come out just a tiny bit shorter each time.  (I have not noticed any shrinking of the waistband; they only seem to shrink noticeably in length, thankfully...)

They're very comfortable pants, with sufficient room in the crotch and thighs to let you sit and crouch and move around without restriction, so I ordered three more pairs in the same exact colors---but this time with a 32" inseam.  I measured the inseams when I received them, and found them all to be a little under 33 inches in reality.  I then washed them, and this time I intentionally dried them in a hot drier to speed up the shrinking process.  Sure enough they are all already a full 1" shorter, at around 32" now.

I expect these 3 new pairs to continue to shrink over the next six months in the normal laundry cycle until they are about 3" shorter than they started, which is 30" and perfect on me.  (That's 3" total shrinkage from the 32" inseam, which when measured was actually 33" to start with.)

So do buy these pants---you'll love them---but buy them 2" longer than you usually wear.  Then just give them time (or a few hot dryer cycles), and they will shrink to your perfect length.

From the sounds of other reviews it appears to me that the closer you get to a 30 waist the more true they fit. So, choose wisely.  Comfortable light material and they seem to be constructed very well. The Canvas really just feels like thin denim. The real reason I'm reviewing these pants is to let my fellow "big men" out there know that if your like me and have bigger muscular thighs and have a hard time finding truly loose fitting pants, look no further. I have tried on dozens of supposedly loose fitting jeans from every brand imaginable with nearly all fitting me like 80's style 501s (or rodeo style Wranglers for the country folks). These are the baggiest pair of pants I have owned since me beloved Silver Tab Baggy and Lucky 48 "Fat Boy Fit" jeans were discontinued. Now if Carhartt would just make this cut in a standard 5 pocket jean with some nice dark washes I be set for life. I do feel compelled to warn all the slim guys out there that, your little birdie legs will probably be "swimming" in these jeans and I'd go with Carhartts "relaxed" fit instead. (A little side note to the big men. I have also found that Wrangler 20X style 33 "extreme relaxed" jeans also fit me and my bigger thighs well)

I like carpenter pants for the pockets - they have more utility than "cargo" pants, for me. To work I've been wearing Wal-Mart store brand carpenter jean, 15 bucks a pair, because I like the pocket configuration and they are cheap, but I wanted something more durable. Wranglers were out - they only have one leg pocket!

These run a bit tight in the waist - I ordered two inches larger than my typical waist size and they fit perfectly out of the dryer.

The right hand side leg pocket has a reinforced seam at the opening, which makes the clip of a multitool or folding knife a bit snug to slip on or off. But it won't get frayed or torn up anytime soon. Typical carpeter pants have a ruler pocket with diagonal opening and a square tape measure pocket on the right side, but these have the reinforced cell phone pocket. It works ok for my purposes, it's where I clip my leatherman tool and stow screwdrivers or wrenches if I need a free hand and don;t want to set them down (I always lose track if I set them down somewhere.)

The left pocket is a more traditional sewn on square of cloth, like traditional carpenter pants. It holds a small flashlight just fine, and a flat cell phone.

These pants have hammer loops on both legs, not just the left leg like most carpenter pants.

The canvas duck fabric is lighter than I expected, which IMO is a good thing, but still seems a lot more durable than the denim you get in most jeans.

I am disappointed at how small the right side "change" or "watch" pocket is, compared o most carpenter jeans. Items that ride comfortably in the watch pocket of my other carpenter jeans either don't fit, or ride up and dig into my side, if I stick them in the change pocket of these pants.

I had three pairs of these that fit perfectly when I first got them, but after several months I noticed my ankles were drafty.  I got out the measuring tape and my nominally 30" inseams (which started out closer to 31") now measured just 28".  This happened to all 3 pairs after maybe 15 laundry cycles.  I wash and dry them in compliance with the laundry label, and they do just fine, but they apparently come out just a tiny bit shorter each time.  (I have not noticed any shrinking of the waistband; they only seem to shrink noticeably in length, thankfully...)

They're very comfortable pants, with sufficient room in the crotch and thighs to let you sit and crouch and move around without restriction, so I ordered three more pairs in the same exact colors---but this time with a 32" inseam.  I measured the inseams when I received them, and found them all to be a little under 33 inches in reality.  I then washed them, and this time I intentionally dried them in a hot drier to speed up the shrinking process.  Sure enough they are all already a full 1" shorter, at around 32" now.

I expect these 3 new pairs to continue to shrink over the next six months in the normal laundry cycle until they are about 3" shorter than they started, which is 30" and perfect on me.  (That's 3" total shrinkage from the 32" inseam, which when measured was actually 33" to start with.)

So do buy these pants---you'll love them---but buy them 2" longer than you usually wear.  Then just give them time (or a few hot dryer cycles), and they will shrink to your perfect length.

Comfortable light material and they seem to be constructed very well. The Canvas really just feels like thin denim. The real reason I'm reviewing these pants is to let my fellow "big men" out there know that if your like me and have bigger muscular thighs and have a hard time finding truly loose fitting pants, look no further. I have tried on dozens of supposedly loose fitting jeans from every brand imaginable with nearly all fitting me like 80's style 501s (or rodeo style Wranglers for the country folks). These are the baggiest pair of pants I have owned since me beloved Silver Tab Baggy and Lucky 48 "Fat Boy Fit" jeans were discontinued. Now if Carhartt would just make this cut in a standard 5 pocket jean with some nice dark washes I be set for life. I do feel compelled to warn all the slim guys out there that, your little birdie legs will probably be "swimming" in these jeans and I'd go with Carhartts "relaxed" fit instead. (A little side note to the big men. I have also found that Wrangler 20X style 33 "extreme relaxed" jeans also fit me and my bigger thighs well)

But it won't get frayed or torn up anytime soon. Typical carpeter pants have a ruler pocket with diagonal opening and a square tape measure pocket on the right side, but these have the reinforced cell phone pocket. It works ok for my purposes, it's where I clip my leatherman tool and stow screwdrivers or wrenches if I need a free hand and don;t want to set them down (I always lose track if I set them down somewhere.)

The left pocket is a more traditional sewn on square of cloth, like traditional carpenter pants. It holds a small flashlight just fine, and a flat cell phone.

These pants have hammer loops on both legs, not just the left leg like most carpenter pants.

The canvas duck fabric is lighter than I expected, which IMO is a good thing, but still seems a lot more durable than the denim you get in most jeans.

I am disappointed at how small the right side "change" or "watch" pocket is, compared o most carpenter jeans. Items that ride comfortably in the watch pocket of my other carpenter jeans either don't fit, or ride up and dig into my side, if I stick them in the change pocket of these pants.

I have been shopping for a dress skeleton watch for some time and stumbled onto the EE Dorado. I'd not heard of this company before, so I checked their website (they are a long-established German watch manufacturer), so I took a chance. This watch is a BEAUTY! It's far and away the best looking "skel" I've found for the price, and if the almost $800 retail price is to be believed (MSRP on watches is highly inflated), then this watch is a steal. The only other watch I was considering was an Android with a metal bracelet (an entirely different look) and at almost twice the price. I did notice there is no country of manufacture shown anywhere on the watch or the packaging. Although this is a German company, it makes me wonder if they are making these in China or someplace overseas. I've got only a few complaints-the clasp is difficult to open/close and the gold hands can be difficult to see (no contrast with the gold mechanism and no illumination). However, I'm so mesmorized by the sheer elegence of this watch, I really don't mind. Beautiful wooden box, too! A real keeper that I'd highly recommend. The vendor was also very prompt with shipping-it even came insured.

I looked for a good deal of time for a skeleton dress watch and I am truly happy I purchased the Dorado. After over 2 years of ownership it still looks great (actually the watch looks better in person than it looks in Amazon's pictures) and hasn't skipped a beat. I am always amazed at the number compliments I get when wearing it. This was my first watch with a deployment style buckle. It took a little while to get used to it, but now I think it's the only style of buckle I'd have on a watch. No more dropping the watch on the floor when trying to put it on and it also keeps the leather strap from wearing out at the buckle. The watch also comes with an impressive wood gift box. All things said I give the Dorado a 5 star recommendation for quality, value and good looks.

I'm a repeat customer for the World's Softest Socks (Over the Calf).  I had been using the "Large" size which fit better than most over-the-calf socks for me. "Fit as expected" doesn't do justice as a fit rating...this pair fits me perfectly, I'm happy to report.  I wear size 15, extra wide shoes....which often leaves me without options when it comes to shoes or socks, hehe.  I hadn't realized that the "Large" size was leaving my toes feeling cramped, after a long day...I thought it was my shoes.  After wearing these "X-Large" with the same shoes...no cramped feeling in the toes.  Obviously, I've been wearing one size too small.  The "Large" size came to just over mid-calf on me, and the "X-Large" come all the way up over the calf  (I've shrunk a bit over the years to about 6ft 3inches).  For everyone tall, with big wide feet, I heartily recommend the "X-Large" size...I know I'm buying more.  By the way, these socks are very well made, and last a long time.  They do come with a good warranty, and I know a couple of years ago, the manufacturer had a little trouble with their quality, for a short period of time.  I'd bought about 5 pairs at one time, and the same sock in each of the packages had a toe seam unravel (before I wore them), but they were quick to replace them for me.  For years before that event, I'd never had a problem with their socks, and since then, their quality has been great, I've found no defects in any of the socks I've bought or received.  These are the best socks I've ever worn.

I was very disappointed to discover Jockey discontinued the Elance Poco mid briefs at the retail level.  I've been buying this style since the early '80s when baseball player Jim Palmer was on the package.  Was told by the retailer that Jockey's "Stay New" #8492 are the model that replaced the Elance Poco style.  They fit okay, but I felt a little shrink wrapped in them.  They are 95% cotton/5% spandex. The deal breaker was the dense stitching around the base of the waistband- it dug into my waist & was really apparent when wearing jeans.  So happy to find out that Jockey resurrected the Elance Poco style & that they are available online.  I've read comments about the fabric being thin, fitting small, causing itching & so on.  I found they are the same for fit & comfort as they were before being discontinued. A smooth waistband & breathable 100% cotton, which I prefer.  From the '80s to present, they always shrunk a little after washing, but fit comfortable.  As for fabric, it is a little thinner compared to when they were made in the USA in the '80s to early '00s.  After the US, I think the manufacturing switched to Mexico, then Jamaica & finally Honduras, where they were made for the final years before being discontinued & continue to be made there for the online versions.  The online versions don't have tags, it's an embossed label on the back panel of the brief, showing the Jockey name, size & where they are made. They come in a wide variety of colours, which is really nice. Haven't seen these in red since the '80s!  Seemed to be black, white & grey that were available at retail in the '00s & early '10s. The packaging isn't the matte plastic cases, like when they were sold in retail. Now, 2 briefs come in a plastic baggie to save on weight & extra bulk for shipping through the mail. I really hope Jockey don't discontinue these great brief because they are the only ones I have found that fit excellent & are so comfortable to wear..

(but i'm sure it will last over a year with daily wear). 2nd, the buckle is not what I expected,  I've only had the slide buckle, but this one is hinged, and does not have the typical slide bar. Perfect for pants with large loops, like jeans.  Not for the dress-slacks crowd or, apparently (previous comment), for people with tiny waists.  I prefer the clamp style buckle, rather than the pinch-bar buckle, because I believe it is more secure and less prone to slipping.  A previous reviewer noted that the clamp style buckle is more bulky than a pinch-bar buckle but personally I don't find it cumbersome, overly obvious or overly heavy for jean use.  I'm a little bigger and taller than most, so I suppose it may be bulky for smaller people.  However, it is no where close to the bulkiness and weight of an average cowboy belt buckle and doesn't have their sharp edges that tend poke you.  It's made by Levi and probably designed for use with jeans, or very casual pants and shorts, so the bucket is not shiny but has more of a pewter finish.  Not having had it long, I can't assess durability factors like web stretch (can be recut shorter though), clamp bite loosening, and oxidation of metal finish.  I would buy more if it came in other colors (i.e., blue and tan).

May, 2013 UPDATE:  I just bought the Olive color version to add to my 2 black ones.  The durability of the black ones has proven to be very good.  They don't slip or stretch excessively.  The buckle finish doesn't show scratches and hasn't oxidized.  The colors of the belts are subdued and look sort of faded by design (not as much perhaps as stone washed jeans are), so don't expect a "Jet" black color to exactly match your new unfaded Black Levi jeans.  So, if your belt loops can accommodate a full 1.5-inch wide by 1/8-inch-plus (<3/16") thick casual-style belt, then this may be for you.  Be sure to remember to cut any excess web strap off on the buckle end of the belt as per the instruction tab on the buckle which will you will, no doubt, tear off immediately.  Excellent belts for casual wear -- but I still wish they came in more colors, like Khaki, grey, and brown.

This is, buckle-wise, the next best thing, and the belt itself is vastly superior. The Wenger Swiss Military Battalion #72456 is a fine example of Swiss quality, craftmanship and precision.

The watch looks great having the black dial and a prominent red second hand that hits the tick marks precisely. The numerals, markings and clarity of the crystal are all sharp. The hands and markings are large and easy to read. The size and weight are just right. The brushed stainless steel case and two tone band are sturdy and the links are easy to remove.

This watch looks and feels like a much more expensive timepiece. The $80.00 I paid was a bargain that I could not pass up. I also own the Wenger 72458 "sister watch" which is the blue version of this watch with a stainless steel watch band. The blue dial version sells for even less @$65.00. However, this one's appearance is somewhat nicer with the gold accents and two tone band. Both watches are 200M water resistant.

This Swiss timepiece is very accurate within 1/10 sec a day as advertised. The packaging is very nice in the elegant Wenger steel case. This is not a throwaway box.

One issue that I did encounter is the stem doesn't always click into the correct position to perform date or time reset. I would rate 5 stars if it was not for this.

Wenger #72456 is a fine Swiss quality watch to add to your watch collection. I highly recommend purchasing this item. You won't go wrong.

This product is outstanding and the price on Amazon can not be beat. Buxton owns the rights to the Dopp name and produces these "official Dopp" kits. The leather is good, feels solid and well stitched, but you can also get them in a slightly less expensive PVC leatherette version. You can also find these in some stores although the ones I found were double in price. Sometimes the bottoms are leather and sometimes the bottoms were a beaded plastic. Frankly I made sure to get the beaded plastic as it will last longer than a leather bottom. The key features if this Dopp kit are: 1) Construction feels solid. (Although the tag says made in China...you would feel better if it had a proud to be made in the USA tag...however, I don't think this is an issue here.) The leather and stitching feels strong. The zipper is a hefty enough piece of metal that will last. The leather handle is small enough that it fits under the fold of the kit's side if you do not want to use it. The inside is a traditional liner with a single razor pouch, however, the liner and pouch feel like they are made of a newer composite plastic material than the older plastic liners these type of kits used to have. The liner feels stronger and I doubt it will rip, which often happened with travel kits. 2) It has Dopp stamped on it, on two flaps/tabs. The tabs are aesthetic choices but look good and remind you that you have a "real" Dopp and not some random "Men's Toiletry Bag."  There are newer types of "Dopp" kit's out there made out of nylon mesh. If you like that I would recommend something by L.L. Bean or Swiss Army. But for something more traditional I would only recommend this brand right here...

I had a Dopp Kit in the early 70's when I was a teenager and somehow lost track of it.  After wearing out the plastic travel bag I've had since then, I wanted to go back to the classic Dopp.  The Admiral did not disappoint - it's a great travel companion!  The sides are a nice, soft leather, the bottom a vinyl which is appropriate, given that the bag will be placed on wet countertops.  The stand-up top stays open for easy retrieval of essentials then securely snaps shut; the bag is closed by a heavy-duty zipper.  Inside the bag is a water-resistant liner with one side pocket for small items. The Admiral Dopp is really lightweight but very well made and stows nicely in an overnight bag - a handsome, high-quality, timeless design.  It's a pleasure when the small things in life work well.

This business card holder is great for my vertical business cards! I'm glad I bought two, because they're perfect for my needs. Here's a quick list of pros and cons:

PROS:
1) It's very professional-looking. The brushed metal on the inside is beautiful!
2) It comfortably holds 14 cards. It could probably hold 15, but I don't want it to be too difficult to get a card out.
3) The product description doesn't mention this, but the top flap has two magnets in it. This magnetic closure was a very pleasant surprise! There's no chance of your cards spilling out in your pocket or bag.
4) The leather part goes all the way around the outside. That wasn't clear to me in the photos. Also, in case you didn't notice, the thread in the leather matches the inside color. Nice touch.
5) For such sturdy construction, it's actually pretty light.

CONS:
1) The colored part on the inside looks soft, but it's really not. Then again, no one's going to be rubbing it against their face, right?
2) The color in the photo (I purchased red) doesn't exactly match the real color. According to the Wikipedia article on shades of red, this is much closer to maroon or rosewood. So if you're trying to match it to your cards or some kind of accessory, be wary of that!
3) When the cards are inside, there's a little bit of extra room to the sides. That bugs me a little because the cards can move around, but I'm guessing it would be harder to pull a card out if the fit were more snug.

This product like most business card cases is a bit larger than most standard business card cuts.  I suppose their use as credit card cases is to blame.  The though is quite nice sturdy enough to protect the cards without becoming to heavy.  The felt lining also helps to protect the cards from the excess room.

This case by far exceeded what I was expecting, especially for this price range.  It actually bests cases that are in the $20-30 range easily.  One person complained about the faux suede on the inside, but not only have I not had any card-sticking issues they mentioned--they glide right out--but that makes it ooze a luxury feel uncommon in a business card holder.

Also, it holds a *surprising* amount of cards for a case this slim.

There are only two negatives I would give it, but even both together aren't enough to remove a star from this five-star review.

The first, the 'pocket' where the cards go has a very high wall to it.  It goes up about half-way up your cards.  Personally I like them to be in the lower-thirds so you can see more of the card, and in cases where you have more than one kind (or other things in there) it allows more 'bending room' to get at what's behind them.  But considering most people will only have cards and nothing else in here, that's not enough of a negative to affect the rating.

The second thing is the magnetic latch.  It's nice and strong, and with the felt-like lining, it opens and closes wonderfully, but it also slides a little to the left and right and I'm always adjusting it when I close it.  Again, more of an I-have-OCD rather than an it-has-a-flaw, which is why again, it doesn't affect the rating.

Finally, because I liked this case so much, I actually now use it as my day-to-day wallet along with a clip for my paper bill money.  I put three or four business cards in it (you always need them with you after all!), then my license, my health insurance card, three credit cards and even a few 'loyalty' cards too.  I can't tell you how many people complement me on it, especially the wait staff when I pull it out, flip it open and remove one of the cards!  I always tell them the wallet is an imported Italian design and they believe me, thinking it's some crazy $50-100!  No, I'm not exaggerating.  More people notice this as a wallet than when I used it for cards!

The bonus of this is the sheer number of colors it came in.  Personally, I like this off-white inside with the black-stitched-leather (faux I'm sure, but it looks great!) outside but I really was tempted by the red for a little flair from the norm. (Classic won in the end however, but I was tempted!)

Again, you won't regret your purchase.  I'm thinking of getting a few more as back-ups.  Maybe I'll get that red one after all!

I bought this watch as a daily casual/semi-formal timepiece that I wouldn't have to worry about being damaged, lost, or stolen. The package arrived in about a week and in good condition, but it wasn't in protective packaging, only wrapped in plastic. Fortunately, the watch was not damaged. At first glance, it has a bit of a Carrera (TAG Heuer Men's CV2010BA0794 Carrera Black Dial Watch) design to it, but without the luxury quality. That being said, everything about the watch case looks more expensive than it really is. The dial details are impressive, with the sole exception of the date window, which is a little too small for the date wheel numbers. Also, the dual second hands aren't exactly in sync, but I suppose this can make the watch look like an automatic chronograph at first glance (auto-chronos usually cost over $1000, so this can be a good thing). The glass scratches easily, which is to be expected with a mineral crystal. The pushers for the month and day functions are good quality, but the crown mechanism is poorly made. It does have three positions: manual wind, date, and time set, but I feel like a few gears are going to break unless I am very gentle with it. The exhibition case back and Krönen & Söhne rotor engraving are nice touches, and the mechanical self-wind movement keeps reasonably good time (gains about 4 seconds per day), though I would be cautious with quality control from a Chinese manufacturer. The power reserve is good, but I haven't exactly measured it. It'll definitely last overnight. The case says it's water resistant, but based on its appearance, I wouldn't test it. It can probably handle a few rain drops but definitely not being submerged. You get what you pay for. The stainless steel bracelet looks great, but the build quality is average at best. The links are loose, and the steel brushing isn't very good, though the double locking fold-over clasp was a pleasant surprise. In retrospect, I probably should have purchased the same watch but with a leather band (Also on Amazon). The watch is eye-catching, and has received a lot of compliments. Overall, for the ridiculously low price (for an auto-watch), this is an excellent timepiece that looks great and performs acceptably.

This is a gorgeous black and gold mens watch. Its an automatic mechanical watch with a style that is somehow both elegant and perhaps slightly fussy with a baroque and steampunk look to it. Its an automatic mechanical watch which means that it does not use a battery.

The front face is lovely. It is a fairly thick plain gold bezel with a slightly convex glass behind which you have a beautifully detailed black and gold face which incorporates many small details. The large clock face surrounds three additional miniature dials that denote the date, day of the week and 24 hours. The main clock face is easy to read with large roman numerals. Oddly 3, 6 and 9 are missing but you don't really notice because the inset border that surrounds the miniature dials tapers towards those points defining those unlabeled hours well enough.

The hands are of medium thickness tapering at both ends in an elongated kite shape. There is a seconds hand which is a needle with a small disk at the pointing end. The hands are inset with some luminous material that glows green in the dark. The seconds hand has only the disk glow while the other hands glow along the whole length.

The crown is golden and nicely knurled with a golden slab on each side. When pushed in, the crown can be used to wind the mechanism. Pulled out, you set the time. Meanwhile the gold slabs at each side are actually mechanical buttons which with each click moves either the date or the day along one position. It works very well and is simple to use.

Automatic mechanical movement

As I mentioned, this is not a battery operated watch. It uses a mechanical winding mechanism. It you turn the watch over, the back plate has a large glass window inset behind which you can see the mechanism. A large half circle center mounted pendulum rocks back and forth when the watch moves. The movement winds the watch. Behind the pendulum you can see some of the inner workings, wheels and cogs rotating and rocking back and forth. Its quite fascinating and very cool.

Other than that you have a black leather strap with white stitching and a simple gold buckle. Its an attractive watch that looks good with almost anything thanks to the black and gold combination. But it looks especially nice peeking out from behind a cuff of a shirt and dark blazer.

In Use

The watch works wonderfully but you do need good eyesight to read the miniature dials for date, day and 24 hours. The detail on the face is great but my husband for whom I got this watch for needs good light (preferably daylight) in order to read them. The main clock face is easy to read which is the main thing.

The instructions state to wind the watch twice a day. My husband found that so long as you wear it and are fairly active you only have to wind it at night before going to bed. The automatic winding through the weighted pendulum that uses your movement works well enough. Pitching it about 20 or so degrees a couple of times is enough to get the mechanism started from stopped. So if you are active it keeps itself wound up quite well. Having said that, you can always wind the crown at any time for insurance. If you forget to wind it before you put it away for the night it will have stopped by the morning and will need the time set again.

Conclusion

Its a lovely inexpensive watch and my husband really likes it. It is a medium size but still qute thick. He noticed the strap is not as big as some, he has reasonably wide wrists of about 7.5 inches and there is only just enough strap to fit a 8 inch wrist and still capture the pointed end of the strap in the loop.

Its a really nice watch that comes in a nice flat dark bronze display box. Its not too heavy and looks really nice. We both like it.

Disclaimer: I received this watch in exchange for an honest and fair review.  The opinions expressed are my own.

Here's my take on all the 1-star reviews for these briefs and why:

I initially bought a 3-pack through amazon.ca (I'm in Toronto), absolutely love them; then found them here on the U.S. site for much cheaper so purchased them again through a U.S. friend's account.

Although the tags of both sport the same product number (R/N# 97404) the better-fitting first set are made in Thailand and are 82% cotton/8% spandex, while the U.S.-sourced briefs are made in Bangladesh and are 100% cotton.

The first set (Thailand ones) sport the classic 2Xist "pouch" and fit the thighs of us bigger guys perfectly, maintaining their shape all day; while the newer designed Made-in-Bangladesh versions have a much smaller pouch and lose their shape in the legs within an hour or two of wear.

Those of us that are fans of the classic 2(x)IST brief need to email the company's head office in Dayton NJ (e2xist@2xist.com) and voice our disappointment at the loss of the original product.

I'm a big polo enthusiast. I wear one almost everyday and am always looking to add a good polo to my collection. From crappy Walmart polos, all the way to Tommy Hilfiger and Ralph Lauren, I own every grade of polo, and this polo held up.

The polo itself is comprised of 100% cotton. It has a nice soft feel to it, but not too soft, as it has a good balance between softness and roughness so that it doesn't shrink too much. The collar is a little thin for my taste. It's not any sturdier than the material of the polo so it doesn't stand up too well by itself. This is a minor annoyance for me, but for such a cheap polo you really can't expect any more.

The sizing is good. When it first came I put it on and it was way to big. However after one was, a little bit of shrinkage occurred (it is cotton) and it actually shrank to exactly where I wanted to it. The polo is a little bit on the "fatter" side, meaning that it's long, but it's also wide. It's built for wider people which may be a good or bad thing based on your preference. Overall the sizing is good though.

As opposed to the previous review, I find I have to wind it twice a day to keep on time -- about ten full winds in the morning and the same at night; otherwise, it loses a couple of minutes each day.  And I don't have a problem with the band -- I prefer non-leather.  The only issue is that it came with two perpendicular straps to keep the tail in place (see photos) and one of those broke for me during the first week or two.
Lastly, the glow-in-the-dark spots on the watch are very dim and don't really work well at night.

Besides all that, though, I really like the watch.  It's hard to find manual-wind watches in general these days without spending $1000, and this one looks nice to me, works consistently, and feels comfortable.  What more could you ask for at less than $20?

Here's the breakdown:

Pros:
Quite (I can barely hear it tick even when I put my ear to it)
Accurate (It keeps time very well and since it's an automatic watch I only have to wind it once in the morning and I'm set all day)
Stylish (I have gotten a lot of compliments on its "retro" look)
Easy to read (The blue against the beige and large numbers make this watch extremely easy to read)

Cons:
The strap is not leather, it's a really difficult to work with plastic (I'm getting a new band).
The hands, though they look like they would glow in the dark, do not.

Once I get a replacement strap this watch could bump up to a 4.5!

The price, quality of Sweater and quick delivery was just what I wanted when I placed the order.  I plan to order more in different colors.

My girls are allergic to metal. Also we have a skin issue where we heal far too slowly (I got my ears pierced when I was 8 and several decades later I still get infections as soon as the earring enters my hole and the hole is red before the earring back is placed behind it, and this reaction gets worse the longer I wear any earring. But I keep wearing them as my collection is too big to really get rid of [I must be some sort of a low level masochist, but my earrings just look so cuuuute!!!...] even plastic earrings send my ears into severe infection), so holes/piercing was out of the question for my girls, who have the same issue with skin healing.
They had been using stick on earrings for a while, but the glue itched and would leave small red rashes if worn longer than an hour. It did not seem to matter what kind of glue it was or who manufactured it, it was a casualty we had to deal with.

These are magnetic! The magnet is large and it holds very well! We were afraid we would lose them straight away, but they stayed long! Also, one child has metal allergy as well and we expected a small earring shaped green dot when she took them off. The metal paint did not react with her skin and she was able to wear these all day without any issues whatsoever! Also, we suffer severe pain for no reason, but pressure makes it awful, so I have to add that these earrings (I tried them myself) caused no real pain to be aware of. This was also a wonderful surprise for all of us after scouring several reviews about how they were too tight. We know pain. This was not pain.

Styling Tips:
We found that when you style your hair first and away from the earring there is less chance of a stray wisp disconnecting the magnetic pull through the ear. Also, metal hair pieces should be placed far enough away so as not to interfere as well. The magnets are very strong! But it is always better to be safe than sorry.

Great wallet. The best I've ever owned. I really wasn't into upscale wallets in the past, but was getting tired of my obsolete-trend design wallet that was also very thick and wide for no reason. I used to keep it in my back pocket but it would give me pain on my opposite butt cheek, so I have sense switch to front pocket wear indefinitely. I also use this technique to ward off pick-pocketers, because nobody in their right mind is going to try to reach inside of your front pocket to gain access to your wallet.

This slim fit, front pocket wallet is excellent because it has a hard leather outer shell. I have owned the wallet for a couple of months now and unfortunately it is bending a bit on the corners, but with the cards inside it keeps the middle crisp and firm. I am glad they did not go with a softer and bendable leather as the wallet would not look as sleek and also be harder to remove from your pocket since it would contour to your thigh, and also generally would not withstand the trials of daily use. The interior leather--I got the eye-catching orange version, which has unfortunately seemed to have been discontinued--is a bit thin and soft for my liking. It is great for being able to easily remove and insert cards, but it seems they may be able to tear more easily and not have enough tensile strength to really grip onto the cards so that they don't accidentally fall out. So far this has not been a problem, and it surprisingly grips the credit cards better than i originally expected.

The money clip is "money," aka genius. It has a locking mechanism that is quite satisfying to click open and shut, and it is just tight enough to hold all the dollar bills you need. The lock is a sense of security and that it will hold every time. I have not dealt with money clips before, but used to think they were tacky or for old guys. This money clip is sexy and modern and minimally elegant. It makes the wallet even lower-profile, since most of the time I am not carrying cash anyway. It is truly the design for the future generation: more credit card dependent and no cash, and not too many "loyalty cards" or coupons.

Sophisticated design and quality product. I also like that it was designed in Australia, because I feel Australians have good taste. I'm not sure where it is made, hopefully in the same country but I doubt it, since it does not advertise specifically.

The gift box is one of the best gift boxes I've opened: comparable to the quality craftsmanship of the iphone box. The presentation is really half the product, and I must confess I bought it because I thought it would be fun to own a small piece of astroturf/synthetic grass. My complaint here is that the grass is cut a bit small and leaves negative space in the box, and seems like more of an afterthought. I would buy this wallet again, but I think mine will last for at least a decade, as that's almost as long as I've had my last wallet, and I'm more proud to carry this one.

-Ken Flemming
Author, "How to Get a Job in Video Games"

This is a good $60 suit. Here are the facts:

- It's Paul Lorenzo suit
- It's off black, which means, it's not the darker black, but about 95% on the black hue scale, more towards brown - this means when seen at light, it's still black, but not as dark. This is due to the material
- Material is the scratchy sort of material. Polyester and Rayon.  I like this material, because it's comfortable without getting hot.
- Inside is lined with black and red trims

Initial fit:
- Good. Jacket top fit well. But at 48 Regular, it was smaller than 46 Regular fit. But plenty of room in the arms, and good for athletic build. Me and my relatively wide shoulders fit in well.
- The arm will be little longer  - for me anyway.
- Pants had enough materials to cut it correctly, which is how the suits usually come, pre tailored.
- It doesn't have any fancy stuff like on the expensive suit, but it wasn't built that bad.
- 48 Regular suit pants came to about 37" - 38" waist. A tight one at that.

I've spent about $70 tailoring it with a professional tailor.

After Fit

Forgot about this: Note: Jacket Pants have 6" drop.  Ouch. This basically means, even after you tailor it, if you don't wear this up on your belly button, your pants are going to feel like MC Hammer's pants, because all of the materials that's there. Most you can take off is about 1/2" before the tailor has to rebuild your pockets, and re-make the pants (basically).

Everything else fit very well.

I like having a slim wallet. My dad's is an inch and a half thick, my cousin's is an inch thick. That's a pain in the butt, literally.

There's 2 money/cash chambers, so you can keep your 100's, 50's, and 20's, separate from your 10's, 5's, and 1's. Or put checks in one. Whatever, there's 2 separate money-holding areas where you'd expect them to be.

There's an ID slot, so you can put your ID in there, and show it to bartenders or whomever easily.

There's not a lot of room for storage of cards, so you've got to be smart about what cards you keep in there - credit/debit card is good, CostCo card is neccesary for those that shop at costco, Sam's club card same deal, medical insurance card, and there's room for a few more. Most places that offer 'membership perks' like grocery stores, REI, etc, you can just give or type in your phone number, and so you stick all those cards in a drawer some place never to be seen again.

If for some reason feel that you NEED those cards, or store business cards in your wallet, this is probably not the thing for you.

This watch looks great, but the quality of the movement is suspect.  My watch was shipped from China in a rather flat, KS branded cardboard box that was badly dented in transit.  Inside the box the watch was nicely packed, and included tags, warranty, instructions, etc.

The KS-095 has a more elegant design than similar Chinese multi-function watches.  The main hands and lower dial (24 hour), are set by the crown.  The day and date dials are set with the recessed pushers on either side of the crown.  The instructions specify the main watch hands be set to 5:30 before using the pushers to not damage the movement.  The case is a reasonable 40mm in diameter, but at 15mm thick, feels a bit clunky. The face looks a bit plastic on very close inspection.  All six hands are inset with a poor quality lume that fades in minutes.  There is no lume other than the hands. The writing and logo on the dial are very sharp, but some of the gold hour indices are slightly skewed off-angle.

The band is made of stiff leather, that is sized for Asian wrists.  I have smaller wrists, but I still need to use the third hole from the end.  It is rather thick, but seems to be conforming and getting more comfortable with age. The band seems sturdy, but only time will tell.  The buckle is low grade (stainless?) steel, and does not match the case's gold finish.  It also must have a low chrome content, and seems to tarnish. The exhibition back reveals a nice looking "turned" Kronen & Shne branded counter weight sticker, giving the appearance of an engraved part.  The rest of the KM0206 movement has rather crudely finished metal parts.

My initial complaint was that the movement sometimes stopped while being worn, and had a poor power reserve.  This watch often stopped running when placed on the night stand while I was sleeping.  The reserve seemed to run 6-12 hours.  I have discovered that while the KM0206 movement is non-hacking, it does allow hand-winding.  Since fully hand-winding the watch, it seems to be working fine (maximum 30hr reserve). Unlike previous automatics I've owned, the self-winding doesn't seem sufficient to keep this model working.

Overall, this is a nice looking watch from a foot away.  It doesn't really look or feel cheap, but its "automatic" movement reflects the price paid.

Update:  The gold plated finish is wearing off in places after less than 1 year of use,  The crown's finish went first, and now the lower case finish is wearing away/tarnishing.  I have managed to clean up both with a Q-tip and some Bar Keeper's Friend cleaner, but the etched KS logo on the crown is now gone and the case is a bit rough where it lost plating.  This is ultimately a disposable watch, and is priced accordingly.  I would suggest choosing the stainless steel option for a longer lasting finish. After recently getting back into the tie game, I began to look for more cost effective ways to round out the tie portion of my wardrobe.

Spending roughly $80 or more for a few ties to get started was acceptable. I needed quality ties in a hurry. And of course, options that are available locally are generally limited.

After some online searching, I came back to Amazon and found the Longtiestore. They had a large selection of ties in colors and patterns that I had yet to add to my wardrobe. I figured for the price, I could afford to take a flyer or two.

I ordered this Navy tie, the blue and gray striped and the coral and navy striped. With the navy tie being the only one I've received so far, I can say that after a full day of wearing the tie. It did what a tie should do. It held a good half windsor and I didn't feel compelled to fidget with the knot after about a few hours because I knew it would hold.

The reason for the 4 star review instead of a 5 star, is that the tie might could have been packaged better. I had to take steam to the tie, to get rid of a crease or two that I'm guessing came from being packaged and shipped. However, this is not really a big deal breaker for me. 10-15 minutes hanging over the shower door with the hot water on full blast did the trick. You could always use the damp cloth and iron method too.

My tie collection is about built out back to where I need it to be. But if the need arises, I can trust the Longtiestore to fill any gaps that arise.

I added a couple of photos to illustrate the issues, but both are serious design flaws.  First, the portion you cut to size the belt frays within about a week after each time you cut it, making the buckle fall off --- So you have to cut about a half inch off every couple weeks to get the belt to stay on.

This means, within a couple months, you now have a belt that's too tight, defeating the purpose of the product.

Ironically, the other side with the clicking notches also isn't securely glued close enough to the notches, which makes it impossible to get the belt off using the quick-release mechanism.  This is difficult to explain with text, but take a look at the photos, and you'll see the design flaws.

After wearing the belt for only a few hours, I have updated my review:
Updated 3-31-16 Reduced to 1 Star:
After wearing with Jeans for about e hrs, I took it off and changed into evening dress slacks and I immediately noticed 5 large cracks in the leather, where the buckle attached to the belt when the buckle was fastened,  so now the belt was ruined and I being an anal engineer, I decided to do a post mortem analysis!

Although the belt appears to be leather it is either a very hard thin piece of leather skin or a thin hard piece of vinyl, skin, as evidenced by the belt not stretching when the buckle was closed, accordingly, it cracked in about 5 places, Investigating further, the core of the belt does not appear to be Leather but rather, some sort of compressed paper or cardboard, with a faux suede lining and the 3 part sandwich was sewn together along both edges, to give the false impression that it is thick leather, Which it is NOT,

The buckle is fine and relatively Heavy Duty so I removed it and threw the leather away, In addition there were left over strings of thread along the sides, left over from the stitching, which I originally had to cut off, Amazon may be sourcing these belts from different sources in China at this selling price point, which may explain why some people are satisfied while others are not satisfied, I did order a more expensive Arthur Italian Leather belt from Amazon, however, it was $27.95 versus $7.99 for this replica belt, so I guess the learning for me was it was way too cheap to be anything but a fake belt,

Original Review 3-29-16: 2 Stars:
The Belt is thick + buckle is rather heavy duty, but leather has a few dent holes in finished side, in addition it is too thick + too wide and very stiff and at 1.5 inches toHD  wear with dress clothes, but rather than returning for a replacement I will just keep + wear with Jeans, I should have known that for $7.95,  it would be a Chinese product with inconsistent quality,

For a very quick introduction, I started looking into hard wallets after having snapped countless cards from using leather wallets. I debated between a fully I closed wallet like this, and the more (currently) common elastic strapped two panel cars holder wallets with money clips. I couldn't decide so I bought one of each, this being the enclosed style. Between the two different styles I prefer this one. I feel like my stuff is more secure being enclosed, but I do have some concerns which I will list in the pro and con list below.

Pros:
#1: Compact
#2: Fully Enclosed
#3: Clicks shut with built in latch

Not sure if this is a pro or con, so Ill leave it in the middle. I feel that this wallet is better off being carried in a front pocket.

Cons:
#1: Nothing larger than a credit card will fit, so forget carrying business cards or those paper cards some places hand out and stamp every time you come in until you earn a free beverage, proof of insurance cards, etc.
#2: It cant hold many bills considering you have to fold them in half twice to fit.
#3: you cant double up cards without extreme difficulty, or stuffing the wallet til it cant close, so you're limited to either 6 cards, or MAYBE 4 cards if you plan on carrying three or more cash bills.
#4: (This is a two for one).... The company that listed this product stated that the wallet is RFID blocking, yet the they include two RFID blocking card sleeves which leaves me wondering if the wallet itself is actually RFID blocking, or if its just the included sleeves that are. Heres the part 2 to this con... those included sleeves? Yeah, they don't even fit inside the wallet, so scratch using those anyway.
#5: The pre installed card slots inside the wallet feel very cheap and Im concerned about how long they will last.
#6: When latched shut, the top and bottom can slide on one another, catching the side walls on each other. (Will try to demonstrate in one of the included photos)

To wrap up:
As contradictory as it may seem to the pro and con list, all in all Im actually (mostly) happy with the wallet. Sure I had to do some spring cleaning when it came to the contents I would normally carry in a wallet, however this wallet allows me to still have my contents fully enclosed, and I don't have to worry about elastic straps wearing out over time like I would have to with the money clip/card holder alternatives. Plus I will no longer have to worry about my cards bending and eventually cracking in half like I have over the last countless years of carrying a standard soft wallet. So if your concerns match mine, then overall Id recommend this wallet.

I was looking for a product to deviate away from a traditional wallet but yet be slimmer than some of the other plastic card holders out there.  I purchased this and while I do like the product a lot, I wanted to share some experiences post-purchase:

-The edges aren't sharp and haven't caused any issues with fingers or fabric, so well done.
-The shiny finish is a bit of a fingerprint magnet, but this isn't a problem for me.
-The case does feel quite secure and the latch is strong.  In addition, there is some noticeable tension when opened / closed so it's not loosely closing.  This isn't going to accidentally spring open on you.
-I've owned this for a few weeks now and somehow I got weird scratches on one side that I'm not entirely sure how they got there.  This wallet never touches my keys and I don't ever recall setting it down on something that could scratch the surface.  It's either in my pocket or on a table.  Take from this what you will.
-Last point, and perhaps most important for you and my suggestion to BRYK.  I feel this device as a whole could afford to be wider; not by much, but maybe a quarter of an inch or less.  Why?  When I tried inserting my cards and ID, the sleeves feel quite firm and restrictive.  I was afraid I was going to make one or more burst at the seams.  Now I'm only inserting 1 card in each sleeve except for one which I'm putting in my ID and two paper-thin insurance cards.  Now if this is to help keep the cards secure and prevent them from bouncing around, then great!  However, if after repetitive use of taking cards out and reinsertion, are the seams of the sleeves going to break over time?  This product does have a lifetime warranty; would that be covered in this type of scenario?  That's a rhetorical question for now, but something for you to consider if you want this product.  If BRYK want to answer that, I'm more than happy to grant them that opportunity.

An RFID blocker is not needed unless you have a "wave and pay" card. Cards that have to be inserted into a reader cannot be read by a remote device. Passport skimming will not yield the information needed to enable identity theft because of preventive measures integrated into the system. The first of these measures is encryption. According to the Department of State: "When a reader attempts to scan the passport, it engages in a challenge-response protocol that proves knowledge of the pair of keys and derives a session key. If authentication is successful, the passport releases its data contents; otherwise, the reader is deemed unauthorized and the passport refuses read access. Additionally, newer passport covers are being lined with materials that block RFID signals from being transmitted when the passport is closed, exposing the document to attack only when it is opened and displayed for a security agent.

I've had this wallet for around a year or so by now, and have a good idea of what I like and what I don't.

Pros:

- sleek clean look that I LOVE
- very durable; I sit on it all the time and it doesn't bend or break
- very slim; again, sitting on it I can barely feel it, and it doesn't stretch my back pocket or anything like that

Cons:

- Metal clasp can be bent. It took me a while to figure out why my wallet sometimes had difficulty keeping shut, but I eventually figured out that the clasp catcher inside the case can get bent. It's an easy fix; you just have to bend it back with a pair of pliers, but it's something every owner should be aware of.
- Not enough space. The holder works for me because I travel light, but the case really can't hold much at all; which is a big problem for some people. I wish it was just a little bit larger.
- Metal will scratch. Not really an issue for me, but mine looked impeccable out of the box and now has scratches all over it. Doesn't bother me, but it should be known. The black version of the wallet is probably much less noticeable.

Overall, I love this wallet, and the BRYK customer service has been excellent whenever I have contacted them. I wish it was slightly larger, but I really can't complain much; for the price I think it's a great product.

The wallet is put together really well. The materials and manufacturing seem excellent. The hinge, clamshell, clasp and rivets are all metal. The only part that isn't metal is the plastic fold-out accordion. The true dimensions are similar to the listed dimensions, with the main difference that it is 20% thicker: 95 mm x 65 mm x 12 mm, and the thickness of the metal is about 0.5 mm. Although the size is slightly more generous than listed, space is somewhat limited due to the plastic accordion. Upon inspecting how the accordion is folded, there are three sheets of plastic between each card slot, which is why people are having difficulty fitting more than 6 credit cards.

For my uses, space is more important than having the flip-out card accordion, so I removed the plastic. It is simply attached to the metal with double-sided tape. It seems like really strong tape, and after removing the plastic it took a bit of effort to remove the adhesive residue using rubbing alcohol. It's almost like a glue. Although I don't have enough cards to test the resulting purely metal case, it seems like you could easily fit more than 10 credit cards without the accordion, and maybe as many as 14. I attached some pictures to my review showing the seams, hinge and product without the plastic accordion.

I don't really understand why people are complaining that it gets scratched. It is made of metal, not diamond. Of course it will get scratched! It comes with a mirror finish, but as you use it, it will become scuffed up. Anyone with common sense would realize this would happen.

The only reason I don't want to give the full 5 stars is because the product does not perfectly match the images shown by the seller. If you look closely on the images shown, there are no seams in the metal, as if it was manufactured by casting. However, in the actual product there are seams along the edges, which makes the wallet much more fragile than if it was cast metal. It is actually manufactured from sheet metal. It seems the images shown are simply CAD renderings, rather than actual manufactured products. I felt like I had been deceived by this, as the reason I purchased it was because it appeared to be cast metal which would have been far superior to other similar products available. It still may be superior to other metal wallets, but it is not what was shown. If the product description was updated with an actual image and not just computer renderings, I would update my review to 5 stars.

The Good
(1) The wallet is packaged in a very appealing way. The box is nice looking and sturdy, and the wallet itself seems to pop when the box lid is opened due to the stainless steel's luster.
(2) Although stainless steel, the wallet lacks sharp edges. As a result of the design, the wallet is comfortable to handle.
(3) In addition to holding credit cards, the wallet is also able to hold cash. I folded 6 bills into thirds, and they easily fit into one of the card slots. The wallet closes quite easily too.
(4) I really like the way the cards are displayedin an accordion like fashion. It makes retrieving the cards easy.
(5) The wallet seems to be guilt sturdy. I really like that it has a lifetime warranty too.

The Bad
(1) The Amazon description says that the wallet holds 7 cards. In fact, it only holds 6.
(2) The stainless steel seems rather soft. As a result, the exterior is easily scratched/marked. These scratches are on the surface onlyvery minor. This is not really a problem for me, but it does  mean that the wallet loses some of that aforementioned luster rather quickly.

The Unknown
I have no way to testing the RFID feature. I can only presume that my cards are protected as advertised.

Because the basic concept of this steel wallet is in minimalism, I knew that there might be an adjustment period in feeling comfortable using this new "streamlined" approach.  However, I personally have found that this new wallet is surprisingly easy to get used to.  In practice, I didn't actually "need" half of the stuff that I always previously carried around with me.

CORE FUNCTIONALITY:
Right now, I've got 5 cards (a driver's license, 3 debit/credit cards, and a transit pass) and a few bills (folded over, of course) all sitting comfortably inside the little accordion-style pouches.  You "can" sometimes fit two cards inside one pouch (assuming the cards don't have those embossed numbers that most credit cards do), but doing so certainly stretches the physical capacity of the pouches, and it becomes notably difficult to insert/remove the cards in this manner.  Advice: stick to one card per pouch (six of them, in total).  As to the RFID protection, I don't have an RFID reader, so I can't really test the protection this wallet claims.

QUALITY/AESTHETICS:
I *love* the look/feel of the wallet.  I read another review somewhere in which someone said it looks like one of those shiny cigarette cases, and that's certainly true.  It just comes across as very...classy.  This wallet also functions as a mirror; seriously, it doesn't just have a decently reflective surface, it is basically of the same quality reflection as a dedicated mirror.  That is, at least when it's brand new.  I'm sure it "can" get scratched up pretty significantly (as I read happened in other reviews), but I've been using it every day for a week, and not a scratch to be seen.  This wallet weighs [empty] 2.8 oz, or the same weight as 12 quarters.  By comparison, my traditional leather men's wallet weighs [empty] 2.05 oz.  So this steel wallet has some heft to it, but by *no* means is it uncomfortable.  I've been carrying it in my front pocket (I was getting tired of the "butt bulge" from my old wallet), and after putting in my pocket, I generally forget it's there until I need it.  I am very impressed with the build quality of the wallet as a whole.  I also have no doubt the stainless steel hinge will last a long time, as compared to those plastic hinges on other hard wallets.

CONCLUSION/OTHER THOUGHTS:
I can see myself using this wallet for a long time to come.  It's ironic, even though this wallet is marketed as a "travel" wallet, I plan to use this wallet in an everyday fashion, and maybe bring my big, traditional men's wallet along in my luggage when I travel, so as to have the most methods of backup resources when away from home base.

Let me know if you have any questions and I'll do my best to answer them!

**UPDATE**

after over a year of use, i have to report that the daily abuse i give this wallet has started to take its toll...

let me be clear:  this wallet still functions, and stays reliably closed.  it has NEVER accidentally opened, and the latch mechanism still performs like new.  also, the stainless steel construction as proven to hold up to bumps and jabs much more admirably than its puny aluminum cousins; there still is not one single dent in it.  additionally, as i had hoped, the year's wear and tear have left enough scratches and scuffs on its surface to liken its appearance to a well-used zippo lighter.

however, it is my duty to inform you good, discerning folks of this product's main weakness:  its hinge.  don't get me wrong, for at least 6 months, when this thing was closed, it was closed TIGHT.  there was no lateral movement of the two sides against each other; everything was aligned perfectly, and it functioned flawlessly.  but, over time, there was enough pressure applied against the wallet to weaken the hinge, which allowed some play and caused one side to offset against the other.  this action causes some grinding, popping noises and makes one wince and grit ones teeth, while one imagines the further progression of this malfunction eventually ruining the wallet's effectiveness altogether.

let me reiterate that while the two sides are quite a bit weaker than when they were new, they still do not accidentally open.  but this wallet is getting tired, and i no longer use it as a daily carry item.

***

the wallet is slim, super mega shiny, and all metal on the action.
the sleeves inside mine are currently holding ID, insurance card, and 5 credit cards; with the insurance card and ID doubled up in one space, that is one space for each other card.  when i push the button on this wallet with it fully loaded as per above, the door will actually spring open; this indicates to me that when closed, there is considerable pressure against the door.  still, after roughly one week of use, this wallet will not pop open on its own accidentally.  i expect the longevity of this latch to outlive the use of the wallet.
i feel it should be noted that the opening mechanism for this wallet is a tab that requires downward pressure to release, and since the tab sticks out from the side profile of this wallet, i fear that it is possible for that tab to be inadvertently pushed as it sits in ones pocket.  nevertheless, that scenario has not occurred in the weeks time that i have owned it.
i would say that in comparison to the more commonly seen aluminum wallets with the curved edges and corners and the plastic clasp closures, this wallet is probably only half as thick, but probably two or three times as heavy; i really like that it has a little bit of heft.  in ones pocket, it remains virtually unnoticed by the wearer, and imperceptible to potential thieves.  all of the aluminum wallets i have owned have had several dents in their surfaces within a week of use; they were never dented so bad as to not function anymore, but still noticable.  this stainless steel one has NO dents in it yet.  i would attribute that to two factors:
1. this wallet is much thinner, therefore it doesnt bulge in ones pocket.
2. this wallet is made of MUCH better materials.  stainless steel will always be stronger than aluminum in equal amounts.
dont go thinking you're going to somehow keep this thing perfectly mirror shiny as it comes; in fact, the finish on this wallet is the part that annoys me the most.  a matte finish of some type would have been highly preferred.  there will be greasy fingerprints on this wallet, and whatever may be left orphaned in your pocket will find its way stuck to your wallet eventually.  my hope is that in time, i can manage to scuff and scratch this thing up enough for it to maybe appear to have come that way.
if you're a fancy guy looking for the proper accessories for a formal occasion, this would be absolutely perfect.  if you're a man who actually USES things, and occasionally may get a little rough, this will hold up to your punishment, but it probably won't look very pretty for very long.  i work construction and this wallet provides excellent protection without getting in my way.

I'm not sure how crucial it is to have each card protected with its own RFID blocking sheath, but it really robs potential room from what could have been a really nice wallet.  On the outside, this thing is tops.  Great lines, good construction and easy on the rear end if you're a back pocket carrier.  It looks more like a cigarette case, IMHO, which is cool, even though I don't smoke.  However, the room inside is a little disappointing, and this little thing is probably made of dark matter, because it's so heavy.  It does not fit everything I need to carry. After seven cards that I MUST carry, that NEED RFID protection(I've been zapped once before,)dental card, medical card and SS card, it barely closes, and there is no room for business cards or cash.  Granted, you don't need to RFID-proof your cash and business cards, but being the pragmatic middle-aged stick in the mud male that I am, I prefer to carry all of that stuff in one location.  Perhaps for someone who only carries one ID, a bank card, warehouse membership card, and small amount of cash, this would be great.  However, I don't think that most men over 30 fit that profile.  Again, the wallet is really cool and well-made, so I give it four stars.  Shipping was super fast, and the product arrived in excellent shape.  However, it's losing a point for lacking room.  Perhaps they could eliminate some of the accordion organizer inside and just shield the outside walls?  Anyway, if you don't carry more than five cards, you'll have room for cash and will probably be pretty happy with this wallet.  However, if you're a normal family man, you probably need something more SUV-like in the wallet department.

It's a nice watch but did not fully meet my expectations. Bought it a month ago.

Design: watch face looks much lighter then I expected. From the pictures it feels that it should be very dark but in reality the top half of the face is very light gray, and the bottom is darker but still much lighter than expected.

Quality: the watch feels very light and fragile. Strap came off, detached from the watch 3 times during the last month, caused by me tightening it too much (wasn't super tight though, it was still wearable with no discomfort at that point). Easy to reattach the strap by hand but doesn't add to the quality feel of the product.

Time keeping: it's very hard to set it more or less precisely. I have to set it up to ~20 min ahead of time for the watch to pick up the correct time. I.e. if it's 2pm then I have to set it to roughly 2.20pm, then it kinda sits there until 2.20pm and then starts showing correct time. And it's hard to figure out the exact offset value.

Date display: the manual says that it comes pre-set for the date to roll-over at midnight. This wasn't my case, it was setup to roll over some time in the afternoon. It's easy to set it correctly but I expected it to work out of the box.

Overall: it's a fine watch overall. I still like to wear it, still looks not bad, and it still shows the time. The time and date setup are documented in the manual so it's not a big deal. But for the price and "german-made" tag I expected more refined product. There are other makes which offer models which feel noticeably better in the same price range.

When I bought this watch, I was in need of a self-winding skeleton-style watch to replace a different one that had broken after many years of use. From the images, this watch looked like a good fit for my style. Once I got it, though (many weeks later, by the way . . . no Prime shippingwhich itself was an indication of troubles to come), there were a few things that didn't seem right. First, Im not sure what the numbering on the outside of the bevel is supposed to represent, but these numbers don't add any functionality to the watch. Furthermore, the small circle on the left side of the face of the watch is just that: a small circle. Theres no secondary second hand there, and its pretty much meaningless.

As for the functionality of the watch, there have been many questions about if the band can be adjusted. The truth is, it can be adjusted, but youll have to take it to a jeweler to do so. There are no adjustment tools included with this watch for you to be able to adjust the band yourself. Unfortunately, this wasn't even the most significant flaw: the watch didn't keep time at all. Usually, Ive had to purposely move my wrist for the first few days of wearing a self-winding watch, but after a few days, itll accumulate enough charge that it will keep time even if Im not wearing it. After a week, this watch wouldnt keep accurate time overnight, even when I wore it to bed. It would also run out of charge mid-way through my day, which shouldnt happen given the activity that I do that normally keeps this type of watch wound up.

As I was searching for replacement watches, the price of this piece allured me, but after my ordeal in trying to return it, the lower price wasn't worth it. A reliable self-winding watch has historically cost me anywhere from $100 to $150, and for a good reason. Aside from the flaws I mentioned above, I was trying to not buy from a brand that seemed to be obviously Chinese. I figured Carrie Hughes sounded like an American brand, but boy was I wrong. When I got the watch (again, after about two weeks of waiting), it came in a package covered in Chinese characters and containing a card typed up entirely in German that I think was asking me to give them a 5-star review. Once I realized this watch didn't work, I went through the painful process of returning it. This process was constantly hindered by what appeared to be a fundamental lack of understanding of the English language. I had to continually be hounding the seller to provide me with the option to return the item (since it wasn't eligible through Amazons normal process), and then had to follow up with them once the USPS tracking number had shown the package had reached them (of which I had to pay for shipping). They never told me that they had received my return until I asked about it two weeks later, at which point I finally was able to get my refund.

In short, if you want something that kind of looks nice, but doesnt function, this watch is for you. Otherwise, stay away!

The fit and finish is mediocre at very best and it doesn't keep very good time but again, what did anybody expect for the price and the cheap auto movement? If you want a decent automatic to get you started on your watch collection I would probably be looking towards Seiko in the $100-200 range, but if you just want something a little larger on the wrist that looks okay from a distance and tells time reasonably well, you could spend the ~$40 in worse ways. Wantdo makes the most comfortable men's underwear I have ever tried (I am over 60)!  Having said that, I would advise prospective buyers that this company is based in China and a bit of patience may be required.  I love their boxer/brief style with a small cloth waistband.  This type has the rubber embossed "wantdo" logo on the outer  front.  I accidentally ordered the boxer/brief with the large "HERO" logo waistband and I returned it as I don't like large elastic waistband, and there's apparantly another style with a large waistband with a printed 'Wantdo" logo.  They have many differing styles under a single page on Amazon's site, so choose carefully.  On top of that, they don't have all styles/sizes in all colors so it's tricky picking out the style one prefers in the color of choice.  Also, when I received my first order, they were XL size.  I had ordered M (medium).  I wrote to the company to arrange a return and received an email from a representative who suggested I first try them on as they were Asian sizes.  To my amazement, they fit perfectly.  I have a 32 waist and usually wear a medium.  The quality of the product makes all this a minor inconvenience and I didn't even mind paying $18.00 per pair, which I have never done before.  Maybe I am just unaware, but I don't know of any American apparel company making underwear of 95% Modal, (a fiber derived from bamboo), 5% spandex (so comfortable!) with a perfectly designed shape to accommodate the male anatomy and look so good at the same time!
