This is my new favorite shirt. A few notes, however:
1. This is a 'slim fit' shirt. If you are looking for a loose or baggy fit, this is not the shirt for you.
2. The fabric is not as thick as the picture looks. Sorry, this is more of a knit shirt than a sweater. If you want something to keep you warm in cold weather, maybe try something else.
3. The collar has to be styled in order to stand up. It's little more than a sewn on flap. You have to fold it inside in order to get it to stand like it does in the picture.
4. Asian sizes run smaller than US sizes. I'm 6'1", 150 lbs, 30" waist with a very slim build and a medium is a casual fit. I plan on ordering a small because I like my clothes form-fitting.
5. Keep in mind that the photo pictured here is on a mannequin with athletic measurements and with a man's face and hands photoshopped on. It will not look like that on you unless you have an athletic physique.
6. The collar is a bit wider and not as tall as pictured, which I actually wound up liking more anyway.
A note about care: Do not ever put this in a dryer, the materials are not designed for it. Add extra spin cycle to your washer and this puppy will come out nearly dry. I took it straight from the washer, hung it up for a few hours and it was ready to wear. Shipping was faster than expected (10 days as opposed to the estimated three weeks)

The only con I have to mention is that the shirt does not come with extra buttons in the event that one becomes detached or lost.

For the price, this is a really great mask. The only significant mark against it is the strap, which was just a little too short to easily tie behind my head. I'm a guy and I have a decently large head, but it I easily fit all medium-sized hats. Anybody with a large head might want to plan to use a pin or clip instead of trying to tie the straps. Small-to-medium heads will be able to get it tied, but might need some help.

The mask itself is lightweight and fit my face pretty well, so it didn't get uncomfortable for a few hours. For most of the night, I forgot I was even wearing it; but after a few hours hanging out and dancing in a warm nightclub, I was looking forward to taking it off. All things considered, I think that's the best experience you can ask for on any mask, so I'm not complaining.

The material is sturdy and definitely didn't strike me as particularly fragile, but it allows for a little bit of flex. I don't think I would try to bend it because it would probably snap with enough pressure. However, I bet it could be reshaped with heat and maybe some steam. I'm not sure if that would cause problems for the glue, though.

Aside from the strap, the only other problem with this mask is how many other people I saw wearing something very similar. It's a very common style and in a dark setting the things that make it look different aren't going to show up at all. If you're looking to stand out, this might not be the best choice, or you might consider further styling the mask after you've got it.

Oh, and shipping was super fast. This mask appeared about a week before I expected it with the free shipping option.

I obviously did not read about this product. I had been looking for a compression tank top for my son and there were many to choose from. I decided on this one because I thought I was going to get 2 in the package. The picture shows two shirts. Two of the exact same shirt. The same picture. Not the front and the back. Not the front and the side. The same picture. Plus- the name of the product has a number 2 in it. Since we were going for quantity and not necessarily quality, we decided on this. I was so excited that we were going to get 2 shirts for about the same price as others were selling 1.
However that is my fault. I should have investigated it more. But oh well now we own it.
My son wanted a compression shirt because he feels that his "moobs" (man boobs) are too big. I can't see them. But he is uncomfortable wearing t-shirts by themselves. He will wear a hoodie even if it is a hot day. He can wear a large or even an extra large shirt. So we thought getting a large would work for him. He notices that if he sticks or Puffs out his chest, he notices the compression more and feels that it is doing its job. But if he is relaxed and just hanging out, he doesn't feel like it is small enough. He wore it the first day, and he liked it. But when the day was over, he really didn't know how he felt about it anymore. And he hasn't worn it since. I think if it was just a little bit smaller it would be perfect. We like that it is a tank top that way he can wear it under shirts. But he will probably have to wait either a few months or a year so he can grow a little bit more to fit into it. So now the search is on for another good deal.

The Shark Sport Watch Model SH159 arrives in a smart red box, nicely embedded in foam and attached to a beautiful leather strap, in a lovely tobacco shade in my case, as I selected the brown option.  One notices immediately that the face is unusually large, so much so that it might even look too big on a man with slim wrists.  On a muscular arm, it looks impressive and certainly eye-catching.

It has an aura of quality and sturdy reliability.  The buttons are easily accessible and work reliably.  The main reading has an hour hand, minute hand and second hand.  On the right is a date display and on the left is the second time zone reading.  Very handy for people who travel abroad, as it completely eliminates the annoying and sometimes confusing procedure of changing to the local time back and forth.  Given the partial dial, this second time reading is approximate as regards the minutes but, for precision, one can refer to the minutes on the main dial. The booklet of instructions covers nine watch models, but the SH159 is not one of them.  I found that the closest model is the QTM2.  In any case, operation is fairly simple.

To change the date:  Pull out the largest, central crown (on the right hand-side) a very small amount (first position) and turn to set the day's number (14 for the 14th day of the month).  Push back to set.

To adjust the time:  pull the largest, central crown out fully (second position) and turn to set the time.  Press back in when done.

To set the secondary time (for a different time zone): Pull out the left knob and turn to required hour setting.  Push back in to confirm.

Stopwatch operation:  the starting position should be zero.  Push the top knob (A) on the right to both start and pause or stop the count.  Press the bottom knob (B) to reset the chronograph hand to 0.

I like the lightness and comfortable feel of this watch on my wrist.  Despite its imposing size, it does not weigh down my wrist and arm.  It looks edgy and reminds me of a rugged Diesel watch.  The quartz movement is precise and the watch does not require rewinding.  The miniature battery which powers its movement is said to last approximately 2 years, after which it should be replaced by an authorized dealer.  It is rated 3 ATM, which means that it can take splashing and rain, but should not be immersed in water.

I love the leather strap, with its easy adjustment (the holes are straight slits, very easy to engage) and I generally like the look and the feel of this watch.  I was asked by the vendor to evaluate a sample watch for review purposes.  The reason I have withheld the fifth star is that, to my ageing eyes, the readings are very difficult to discern.  The hour and minute hands are grey over a black face and the only stand-out hand is the yellow second hand.  Also the main watch dial only shows numbers for the hours 7, 8, 10 and 11.  The other positions are a matter of guesswork.  It is actually easier to read the secondary time as the digits are printed out, grey again for the main hours and yellow for the half hours.  If this watch had been designed to be easier to read, it would have scored top marks with me.

For most of you this is your grandfather's rugby shirt, or great-grandfather's, the type they then modified for shoulder pads and it became the original football jersey.  Heavyweight knit, triple or quadruple or something, reinforced everywhere with taped seams or reinforcing stitching, like under the arms, rubber buttons, heavyweight cotton canvas collar--this thing will fade long before it wears out, and I don't expect it to fade before 2050 or so.  This is not your nice lightweight summertime long-sleeve polo.  Huge out of the box, shrinks to size after one wash and dry.  It'll soften over time, and become your favorite.  One tip for the manufacturer and buyers: the cuffs are also original heavyweight cotton knit: no spandex or whatever.  If you expect the cuffs to stay shoved up your arms you better have huge forearms.  Wonderful shirt.

This ring feels nice most of the time. I was really disappointed by the lack of half sizes. I require a 7.5, but I had to buy an 8, which means the ring fits me loose. In normal circumstances this isn't a big deal, but when I am washing my hands, or taking a shower, the ring gets really slick, and I have had it come off a few times.

The ceramic portion of this ring is fantastic. It looks beautiful, and it extremely well-polished. I have gotten compliments from strangers on the beauty of it. However, since it is so well-polished in the inside, it does have a tendency to be sort of sticky. It's a bit difficult to explain, but if a very small amount of perspiration gets between the band and the skin, it's almost like a suction or vacuum which causes the ring to pull on the skin. It isn't painful or anything, just a bit uncomfortable, and is cause for constant adjustment, which then becomes an annoyance. This may also be due to the fact that it is a little too big for my finger.

The carbon fiber portion was unbelievably beautiful in the beginning. The criss-cross pattern of the fibers reflects light beautifully. The resin is completely transparent, and polished to high gloss, and so smooth and level with the ceramic that it is difficult to distinguish where it ends. There is very good craftsmanship in that. The problem is that it is resin, and so after a few months the scratches begin to build up, and the resin is no longer transparent. I have had this ring for three months, and it still looks good from a distance, but the resin is starting to take on a translucent quality from the scratched surface. Eventually the carbon fiber strands will be hidden behind the scratches, and will need to be polished.

With all of that said, this ring is still very much worth the money. After all, it is very inexpensive, and you can afford to buy a few of them now, to replace the ugly ones in the future.

I haven't experienced any chipping, cracking, or breaking, and the ceramic is extraordinarily difficult to scratch.

Great price and takes a beating... still shining good as new. I should be able to get paid for torture testing jewelry at this point in my life. Nothing really lasts long enough to be considered old but so far this ring has laughed at everything I have thrown at it. To date it has survived spray paint, acetone, grease, gasoline, soldiering iron, various hand tools, solvent products and gun cleaning brushes... Guess what? Still shining... I will update in a year but so far I am completely impressed.

This is a handsome looking watch, make no doubt about it, both in pictures and in person.  I was nervous about many things with this watch, especially buying overseas, but they were all placated once I received the watch.  It came in a simple box with a pillow, but no instructions.
 - The crown is a screw-in kind, but the second hand does not stop when you pull out the crown all the way to set the time.
 - It keeps time pretty accurately, haven't measured it exactly to the minute though, but it hasn't really gone too far ahead or behind in the 4 days I've owned it.
 - It doesn't look too big on the wrist, in fact it looks really good.  The case height is relatively high but I can fit it underneath my shirt cuff just fine
 - The strap is nice and the clasp is just okay - it's kind of awkward to set up, but it is nice to have a clasp.
 - The bezel rotates counter-clockwise.  I have seen a few videos where the bezel has been messed up in one way or another with a Parnis, so I was nervous mine might not align perfectly at the 12oclock position or it would be too loose, but it ratchets quite nicely, and lines up perfectly.
 - The movement is a 21 jewel Miyota movement (which I assume they mean Citizen?), and it works fine - I estimate 4-5 ticks per second, so it isn't the smoothest in the world, but it also definitely gives the effect of a smooth ticker just fine.
 - The weight to wind the spring is a bit loud - not louder than the vents in my office, but in a quiet room you can hear it for sure.  I can't hear it when it's in the watch winder though.
 - The crystal is sapphire, which is very nice

I purchased the set of 3 gold Huggies because I wanted the largest hoop to wear as my everyday earring. When they arrived, I found 2 of the smaller hoops had fallen out of the spongy slot but they were not damaged. I immediately knew that any hopes I had that the medium size hoops may also work for me went out the window. They were too small for my taste. Nonetheless, I was happy to get a pair that I could wear after spending around $10. The curved stem of the Huggies is indeed a bit harder to put on than straight ones but itr wasn't too bad. My left ear piercing is a bit lower than the right one and a bit enlarged as well so the huggie doesn't hang as pretty as the right ear. I found the weight of the 16mm huggies to be quite satisfactory. The comfort with huggies is above most other styles of earrings. I don't like to switch out my jewelry on a daily basis. I also like to wear them in the shower, swimming, sleeping, talking on the phone, etc.  So, comfort is of utmost importance. These pass the test with the exception of swimming. I haven't done that yet. I hope someone who has worn them in the pool will let me know how they hold up. My only complaint is that the inside of the hoop isn't polished like the outside because you can see the inner hoop very easily when wearing the 16 mm one.

Don't be fooled. These aren't exclusively for men. I found them while looking for sterling hoops and I'm glad I investigated them more. After reading about them, I realized they would be a better option than silver because of the low maintenance. While I do still love silver, there's always the pesky task of cleaning them when they tarnish. BEHOLD! No special care needed with these earrings. At least not yet that I've noticed. If, in the future I find that they do need some special maintenance, I'll edit my post.

Here's what I love about these:
1. Varying sizes. Want something understated? Go with the smallest size. Have more than one piercing in an ear? Add others!
2. Easy to insert.
3. Comfortable. Even while sleeping.
4. Pretty secure. You don't feel like they could fall out unknowingly.
5. Nice finish.
6. Great price!

What I don't love:
1. I found that some of them clasp more tightly than others with an audible click. It seems like the holes or end ball aren't uniform. I am a little leery that one could come unclasped but it's not a huge concern because the whole earring would have to be severely jostled to come out of your ear. I don't know how much of a problem that would be for most people. I don't wrestle, play rugby, wear helmets or do any other activity where my head gets bashed around. And if I did, I'd probably forego earrings.

Overall I'm very satisfied with these. Hopefully my review helps someone :)

I have been looking for some huggie earrings. I had my ears pierced many years ago, and haven't worn earring for a few years, so getting my ears accustomed to having posts in them again has been a struggle. Sleeping with post earrings is a mess. Posts always poking into my neck. So huggies looked appealing due to the design of the post wrapping into the inside of the hoop. (Many don't offer this particular design, you have to put the post into a very small hole on the end of the hoop). Got these yesterday and put them on. Easy to put in, they are hinged, so you drop the back side down, slide in the post, lift the back up again until you hear a tiny "click" and done! No more painful post pokes! Slept in these without a problem. They are 9mm inside and 13 mm outside, and there is about 1/4" from the inside of the hoop to my ear. This is a very handsome, vintage-style watch that has cool Gilded Age/Edwardian vibe.  The color is made to look like that of polished brass but it is not. The watch feels much lighter than it looks and won't weigh you down if carrying on your person or in your pocket.

A ring of Roman numerals are inscribed on the inner ring while the outer ring has a nice embellished floral design motif. The time is a little hard to read because the window is small (about the size of a dime) but you can pretty much figure it out by the way the hand points toward one of the Roman numerals. If you press down on the top knob, it opens and you can see it much better. It comes with a matching chain that has the same antique feel as the watch.

The windup mechanism is pretty cool because you don't often see windups these days (no reliance on batteries!) and there is a bigger picture window on the back through which you can more clearly see the gears moving around.  Very cool.

It's handsomely packaged in a brown box and the watch rests on a velvet cushion. Very classy and I always like how Mudder packages their products.

Overall this is a very fun watch that is convincingly antique for not a lot of money.

One can opt to purchase any one of the many faux leather wallets from you local department stores, glued and heat pressed together, or you can go for the more hand-crafted look such as provided here from Tiding. I like this more natural look, and give it a thumbs up.

As seen in the listing pictures, this wallet has three sections with the center section being stitched in containing additional credit card and ID slots. Not really a true tri-fold design so it is thinner (thankfully) than some tri-folds; it has three horizontal card slots in each wing, three horizontal slots in the center portion, and a "photo slot" in the center portion into which my driver's license easily fits. All of the slots are made with enough space to fit any credit, debit, or convenience card that I have...

This wallet really does have a great look & feel to it. At 4.25 inches long (folded), 3.75 inches tall, about 3/4 of an inch thick, and weighing in at about 2.7 ounces (per our postal scale), it is not the smallest wallet in my inventory but it is one of the nicest looking and seemingly best put together (nice, uniform stitching).

If you are looking for a wallet of this size, style, construction and price, for use as noted above, then we would recommend giving this wallet from Tiding a try based on my experience with it.

Recommended.

UPDATE (1/21/2015)

As of wearing this soft shell in the upper Northern states for a winter, I have to confess that these pants are terrible.

-The material absorbs water. Not even remotely water repellent.
-They aren't very warm. My poly-pro underlayers are warmer than these.
-It does little to help against wind. It helps slightly, but not much.
-Impossibly small to wear, even for a larger size.
-Pockets. What the heck? No back pockets. The cargo-pockets are microscopic. The actual pockets at the hip are zippered and designed to carry maybe a small wallet and little more.
-Fabric. Is stretching and giving-out after wearing the pants for little more than a week or so.

SUMMARY.

Listen, if these are fabricated with "Asian size" in mind ... DON'T SELL THEM TO AMERICAN CUSTOMERS. Most Westerner customers do not like skin-tight clothing. The workmanship is shoddy,
the material is flimsy, and the product doesn't even live up to it's stated function: water proof, wind proof, warm. In the end, it's just a really crappy pair of pants that are

I finally qualified for my Player King of New York City card, placed it delicately into my wallet, and then immediately realized that this simply wouldn't do. The brilliant glow of the card seemed dampened by old, overstuffed wallet (from the George Costanza collection). This dingy wallet was way too large, way too bulky. I had to find something thinner, more sleek, and more worthy of holding the credentials I had worked so hard to obtain. That's when I stumbled upon the Hammer Anvil Men's Genuine Leather Slimfold. I'm sort of in awe that this wallet costs eight dollars. Sure, it looks a little cheap at first, but after it wears in, it's fine. I've examined the stitching with my jeweler's glass for flaws. I have found none. So the quality is perplexing when I consider the money I spent, but there's something even more amazing about this wallet: the design. This is, quite simply, the best-designed wallet for my needs I've ever seen. I'll break it down. This is the perfect wallet design for urban types. I am always in a city (could be San Francisco, New York, London, etc.). I must have a front-pocket wallet. This wallet has the best arrangement of pockets I've seen while maintaining its slim profile. There's a clear pocket for credentials/ID. There are three card pockets for your debit card, your bank credit card, and your AMEX Black. There's also a larger slot behind these cards where you can stash the ancillary cards you rarely use, like insurance cards, medical marijuana ID's, various underground poker room membership cards, and the like. The kicker is there's an equally large slot on the outside that's perfect for all your rail passes and hotel room keys. The bill area is large enough, but keep in mind that fewer large bills will maintain the slim profile more than many small bills. I'd pay a real wallet maker lots more money if they created a wallet with this design, but they don't, so you should just buy 20 of this one.

I performed the same tests with both wallets, using security badge proximity readers of different frequencies and manufacturers--HID systems and S2 systems.  They all went right through this wallet no matter what pouches I put the cards in.  It never blocked a single read attempt.  The old wallet blocked every read every time.

My husband and I are both vegetarians. And this wallet is a nice, classy wallet without being made of animal materials, which is seemingly hard to find.

Right away I was very impressed with the quality of the materials and the craftsmanship. You could really tell that this was a nice wallet from handling it. The color of the cork and the texture all made it look quite classy.

Upon first observation my husband was a little nervous about the larger size of the wallet being that it seemed bigger than he had pictured. In fact, it is quite a bit larger than the US dollar bill, as shown in my photos. I believe that it's just going to take a little time to get used to having a bigger wallet than he was previously used to.

Early on, it does feel a little bit stiff getting cards in and out of the slots (particularly the second slot as the bottom slot completely covers it). This may just need to loosen up in time.

While It's too early to tell how well it will hold up to long term wear, we are pleased with what we have seen so far, as the craftsmanship is of such high quality. But we will come back to update if anything goes awry.

Bottom Line: This is a fine, classy looking larger wallet. As long as the size is something you can handle, I highly recommend it.

In leaving this feedback, my hope is that Amazon will ask if the hat fits. Well Amazon yes, yes it does-but that is the only positive part of my recent order. The order itself was two days late. Not a HUGE deal, other than this hat purchased as a river hat that was hopefully going to accompany me down a sunny section of the Colorado River yesterday. I adapted though, these things happen.. A lot it seems with Amazon these days, but they still do happen...

Now for the quality of the hat which is what most people are interested in when looking at reviews... The hat fits really well. Snug, but not overly tight. I wish that I could provide more quantitative information because everyone's head size/shape is a little different, but for me it fit nicely.

I have been in possession of this hat for exactly 20 minutes and upon delivery I immediately opened the box. Upon inspection, the hat had 2 tears in the top of it as you can see from the pictures. They are not HUGE tears, ~2" but how long do you really think this hat is going to last considering that it is ALREADY torn and has not even been worn (I should have rhymed this entire review for your reading pleasure...) The package itself did not seem to be damaged, and the hat had had a plastic form inserted inside the hat for shipping that was meant to keep its shape. And it did. Therefore, I'm guessing that the damaged hat was packaged and shipped as it was.. Not good-amazon quality control, not good...

I will be returning the hat today, and I have cancelled my Prime membership. There is just no value in Prime when I continually get packages late or receive products that I just need to return anyway. If this was an isolated incident, I would let it go. It's not, so I can't. I would say with regards to the hat, roll the dice. I read the reviews, I saw how many positive reviews there were, and I felt comfortable enough to order it myself. You may get lucky, or you may not. If not, Amazon is a good enough company to refund you and fix the issue. All you will be out is time, effort, and just a little bit of your soul... (ok, maybe that was dramatic, but it is still a huge pain sometimes returning crap that should have been inspected BEFORE it is shipped)!

There are two approaches to designing and producing  a sun protective natural fiber straw type hat:  The way Tula does it using time honored quality materials and craftsmanship and the  way O'neill does it with the MBA/ California style of anything goes and we hope it works.  This hat fit good and I really liked it until I discovered its 2 big flaws.
  2.  The straw is really cheap and the fibers break up from one wearing on a  motor boat  whereas my Tula hat lasted for years of wearing on land and water
  1.  To compensate for cheap material and cheap workmanship, O'neill installed a liner under the entire brim to block the sun because the straw does not.  That part works but they put no liner under the crown, perhaps to save money on labor or because they were dumb to figure out how to do it or to make the hat cooler.  This hat is a medical device in that it is represented to protect the wearer from the dangers of sun exposure and the standards by which it is reviewed need be very high.  Wearing this hat by any wearer who does not have a dense coat of hair on the top of their head exposes the wearer's scalp to sun exposure and damage.

It's not my style to leave glowing reviews after opening an item. No matter how something looks, it should be durable and practical, something that cannot be done after a several-weeks trial. I purchased this very wide-brimmed hat in 2015 and wore it all last season, and it has held up very well into this summer season (late July 2016). Although the inside of the brim is lined with a dark (in the case of my hat, "Sonoma Stars" red/white/blue) fabric, I feel that this adds the right amount of stiffness and durability to the item so that it does not easily flap around in the wind; it may also make it a tad warmer, as others have noted. In my view, though, the extra stability is worth it to protect the wearer from the sun. The straw weave and chin strap have held up well, and all stitching has remained intact. I purchased it initially only for use around the exterior of the house (I thought its flamboyance was not the style for this staid, elderly gent) - gardening and mowing the lawn - but this year I have dared to walk downtown wearing it and I have received lots of compliments on the hat. My days of only wearing a baseball cap with a visor in front for sun protection, are over.

Note that of the hundreds of reviews left for this O'Neill hat few, if any, are left by professional reviewers in the Amazon "Vine Program", a program that has trashed the integrity of Amazon's review system. People who are in the business of being sent as much free merchandise as they can get their grubby hands on to write creative reviews for products they may have only looked at but not used, cannot be "unbiased" as they purport them to be. I don't know whether they sell their free stuff through eBay stores, save them for giving as gifts, or dispose of them at garage sales, but their mere existence has gotten me to reduce my formerly large volume of online purchases and get back into brick and mortar stores to check out quality for myself, before I buy, as I feel like a chump for being one of the few people to pay the asking price for online goods. I do applaud Amazon that they do identify which reviews are written by these people who receive free items. Sorry for this editorial paragraph, but I had to get this comment off my chest. Amazon should note that this is a Verified Purchase by me.

This sea straw holds up better than the thin stuff they use on the new style of straw hats, much stronger stuff. A month of rough use and no damage at all so far.

The underside has a glued black cotton (I think) layer to help keep tiny sun spots from shining through the straw, making this hat less distracting than my last straw hat. The inside has a thin elastic band to make it fit more comfortably, no more straw poking my forehead.

The chin cord looks frayed, like it was "brushed" to look old like they do with "fashionable" jeans these days. It's softer than most cords because of this (less itchy on chin), but I'm concerned it might have reduced the cord's lifespan.

The brim is so wide that it reduces head range of motion if you're wearing something bulky on/around your back/shoulders (backpack, lifevest, seat/chair, costume) but is very light and comfortable otherwise. Good for yard work and beach, not good for kayak fishing.

The emblem on the front is ugly and prevents air from moving through the front of the hat, but you can cut the stitching on the back, and the glue they used is so soft you can gently pull it off from there without hurting the straw, no heatgun required.

One Year Edit: I still use this hat one year later, I've found it expands too much when it gets soaked so don't use it in the rain it will expand enough that it no longer rests on your head but on your ears, and is heavy when soaked with water. Leaving it to dry it shrank back to the original  size though.

The steel eyelets for the chinstrap are not stainless or coated, they rusted in the presence of salt water (ocean use). If you take this hat to the beach I suggest you rinse the eyelets to keep them from rusting too much. The chinstrap stopper has a steel spring that has rusted too, but it still works so far.

Otherwise, this hat has held up well enough for a straw hat, imo. The only damage is on the very top, and I blame myself for smacking it on things, because I'm used to being short enough to go under, and the hat increases my height several inches.

This is a decent hat and I'm torn about the review. Some aspects are great, others are very lacking. Let's start with my head size, I wear a 7 3/8 - 7 1/2 fitted caps (bigger noggin, but not enormous). In regards to the hat, the black fabric under the rim really helps reduce glare (I used the hat at beaches and many pool decks and can attest to this) but, it only comes in one size and that one size is a bit too small for my head. I realize my large dome is my problem and this hats fits most people well or even a bit too big. But, the rim of the hat sits funny, got oddly molded in the box it was shipped it (which was too small for the hat) and it's never really recovered to normal. The bill has always had this weird ridge in it right where it meets the top part of the hat, and it sits unevenly. I've been battling with the bill of this hat since day one to try and get it to sit normal in a nice disc shape. But, the strap is nice, the padding on the inside of the hat that goes around your dome to prevent scratchy straw on your skin is also a nice touch. If you have a big dome or like your straw hats to sit nicely and not warp and get bent out of shape, you may want to try buying a handmade hat from someone at a local farmers market....at least that's what I had to do.

UPDATE: After about 2 years this hat started to break down considerably, should be noted that it did get worn about 1-4x a month and bumped around occasionally in the house with the hats, but nothing abnormal. It's a straw hat so some of the breakdown was expected and none of the holes prevented it from being used properly (unless you have a bald head in which case it could cause a weird sunburn...luckily my hair is long). But, the woven hat material became very fragile after a year or so and started easily breaking off from touching almost anything after about 2 years.
Good luck!

I work as a crossing guard during very hot, peak sun hours of the day. I have the misfortune of being pale skinned and I also walk to and from work, so I needed more than just the shade around the eyes for an hour. This hat works perfectly. The inside is lined with black fabric, so the glare from the reflective material used in the crosswalk is hindered quite a bit. The fabric also keeps the sun from coming through, unlike other straw and fabric hats. In addition, this hat is very stiff, keeping my field of vision open so that I can see all around me. The cord does a fine job in high wind conditions, and the bead in the cord is spring loaded, so it does not slide down after wearing for a while, but stays put. The upper crown of the hat is not lined, but their is a band just the inside of the crown for sweat absorption. Not having fabric in the top of the hat is helpful for keeping the head cool.  I was initially hesitant to purchase this hat, as my head is large for a woman, and I was afraid the brim would only cover a small portion of my face like other hats have. This is not the case. The brim is 5.5 inches wide, and covers my face, neck, and some of my shoulder when directly under the sun. The depth of the crown is about 6 inches deep, 6 1/2 inches wide at the base, and 8 inches long (since the crown is not rounded, but oblong). I am not sure of my hat size, but the circumference of my head is about 22 inches, and the fit is not quite snug. I do, however, wear my waist length hair in a bun on the top of my head when I work, and the bottom of the crown comes to rest just above my brow. This makes the hat snug for me. Overall, the hat seems pretty durable: the straw is very stiff, and high wind, heat, and moisture have not caused it to bend at all. I believe the fabric lining also keeps it sturdy. I should caution, this is not a hat for fashion, but a reliable utility hat. If it breaks down, I would purchase the same one again, but I don't see that happening in the near future.  A very good product overall.

So I read a lot of reviews about this Pea Coat before I decided to purchase it, and I was extremely nervous going with the size I actually needed instead of a smaller, due to the large amount of review about the coat fitting somewhat large. I am a 3XL kind of guy, so a jacket being too large on a large guy is weird and unattractive... As far as I can tell, the jacket fit perfectly! it was loose enough to fit a hoodie underneath for the colder days, but tight enough where it gave me a full range of motion without swimming in my coat. I live in Wyoming, and our winters can be quite a bit nippy, but this jacket was perfect for me on the days where it lingered in the 30 degree range, and a hoodie underneath would leave me comfortable down into the teens. It is stylish, and the buttons are sewn on well. I also appreciated that it was a good length, I have had poorly made pea coats in the past that hadn't properly covered up my backside when I bent over, and... being a large man with issues of a revealing lower backside... this coat covered things up so I didn't feel so uncomfortable... My only complaint would be that one of my pockets already has a hole in it, but I do utilize my pockets, and it could have been I just put something too heavy in there, so that can chalk up to user error... not manufacturing flaws. I purchased the jacket back in November 2015 (It's now April 2016), and I have used it frequently and heavily. It's a great jacket, and if you are a larger man trying to look nice, this coat will do the trick. It doesn't hide the fact that you own a pet if you have one, though... But that is also something that is chalked up to user error.. dog hair + dark wool coat = hair galore... It's a great coat, and if you are seriously looking to buy one, I'd recommend giving this one a try

My first test with a new pair of pants is always to assess comfort at the extremes. So I put them on and then do deep squats. I am talking ass to the ground squats. These pants handle that well. No pinch spots, no choke points. I also did some stretches with my legs wide out sideways and also out far front to back. You know, just in case Ninjas jump out from behind a bush, I need to know if I will be able to kick them in the head. These pants held up well and stayed relatively comfortable. Now I will not really do a lot of deep squats while wearing these, and I do not fight Ninjas on a daily basis, but I need to know the limits of the pants I wear. These passed my test.

UPDATE:  7/27/18  -  I recently contacted the manufacturer of this watch and was told that it has been discontinued.

I have no idea why, since the HDE solar watch is an excellent value.  Amazon has sold out and Ebay has only
the yellow version of this watch left, and in limited supplies.  I purchased another one and two grey ones over
the past few months so that I have several of them for future use.

After several years I still say that this is the best value in watches on the market.  They keep great time,  have
several useful functions are only need a battery replacement every few years.  They are a tremendous value
and it's unfortunate that HDE has chosen to discontinue them.

UPDATE:  4/17/18 -  I just purchased two more HDE solar assist watches.  After several years of ownership and use,
I still highly recommend these watches. Given their reliability, practicality and affordable price, in this consumer's
opinion, there's nothing out there that can compete with them.

I've been using HDE solar power watches for several years now and I don't think that there's a better value in a watch to be found anywhere in the market place.  In reality the HDE is a solar assist powered watch, since it has a button cell battery that is constantly  recharged by the solar collectors on the HDE.  In my experience these batteries last about two years under constant use before they are no longer able to hold a charge.

You'll notice when they start to fail, because some of the watch functions will no longer operate properly.

Fortunately, the batteries can be purchased in volume packets so that the cost of each battery is around twenty cents, and watch kits which contain the tools needed to replace watch batteries can be had inexpensively.  If you consider how much you'd spend just to have a  jeweler change the battery in your watch, a watch kit can pay for itself in the one or two visits that you would make to a jeweler.

Moreover,  these  watches are more durable than one might imagine.  I've accidentally banged mine around on more than one occasion and they stand up well.

They also keep good time and have useful functions including:  both military and standard time,  the day of the week in both written as well as digital format, a stop watch, a programmable timer, and an internal light which can be activated with the push of a button, and which lasts for several seconds.  This is great if you like to walk or jog in the evening so that you can monitor how long you have been exercising.

The HDE is also water resistant.  That does not mean to go swimming with it. However, if you accidentally get the watch wet while you are washing your hands, you won't damage it. TL;DR: Slim, well-made wallet that can take abuse.  Holds only what you need and not much more.

This wallet is simple and, as such, has a slim form factor, which is what I prefer because I wear my wallet rather than carry about a purse.  If you use the side with the pouch to hold a lot of coins, it can get fat (and heavy).  The card access from the top is great for holding a few cards, but not much more than that, and there is no way to organize if you are trying to carry more cards.  I typically carry just one credit card and my ID in the center card access part.  The internal card holder (the one in the pouch) is difficult to use (especially if you have coins in the pouch) and I do not use this one very often.  This wallet is beautiful and well made.  It has held up to constant abuse (I am not nice to my utilitarian things) and even after all this time there is not one loose stitch or busted seam.  The wallet feels a little plastic-y, but that is fine by me.

If I have any complaint about this wallet, it would be that it is inadequate to hold receipts, which is unfortunate for me because I save my receipts religiously.  It means that instead of having a wallet of receipts to clear out once a week or so, I have to be sure to file receipts every day from my pockets, which is inconvenient, but worth it to have a slim wallet profile.

I considered going with leather for more durability, but this seems quite sturdy, and the colors/picture are very unexpected and unique.

My only complaint is that U.S. bills can be a bit of a tight fight in the bill pocket, so it can be difficult to quickly stuff multiple bills in at once--first time using it, I got $4 back in change and it took me an awkwardly long time at the register to put it away. But overall a good buy!

I thought I could swap lenses and putting the brand name lenses on the cheap one but I compared the lenses and noticed they're very slightly differently shaped, so no matter how much I tried, it just didn't fit. I showed my wife the sunglasses side by side and asked her which one is the real one and her first response was "what do you mean which one is the real one".  She couldn't tell at first glance.  The replacement lenses made the brand name one stand out but I know if the replacement lenses were able to fit in this cheap one, I know she probably could have never tell.  She kinda got mad at me for buying the expensive one lol.  Anyways, I'm very happy with this purchase and if it ever broke I would buy another one in a heart beat.  I saw other sunglasses these seller is selling with similar styles as brand name ones and I would probably get the cheap one than get the expensive one.  I just want nice looking sunglasses that protect my eyes from UV, sure it may not be polarized, but these cheap glasses does a good enough job for 10 times the price cheaper.  I only have one brand name sunglasses and I've owned a few cheap sunglasses but this by far are the best cheap sunglasses I ever bought! I am a girl and I like men's wallets. They are smaller, more practical, more discreet and just plain nicer. I don't want a shiny, huge, pink wallet that will carry the kitchen sink (as a girl, in theory, I have a handbag that can do that -- but I don't, either): I want a to-the-point wallet that will take currency, credit cards, my driver's license and a couple of receipts. No coins, no checkbook, no whatever else women carry in those huge wallets. And on days when for some reason I don't carry a handbag, they will fit into my front jeans pocket or interior coat pocket.

I've been using zippered wallets for years, for the simple reason that I like it that stuff never falls out (I can do a great job of misplacing cash and credit cards on my own, thank you). There have been previous incursions into Amazon's apparently bottomless stash of zippered wallets. The wallets were okay, but with too many divisions, pockets, little nooks and crannies that ended up making them too large, too thick, too bulky, too complicated. And one of them had way too much padding, so even empty it felt huge.

Enter the Mancini wallet. It is zippered. It is small. It has RFID -- I'd been using those little RFID envelopes for my credit cards, but an RFID wallet is so much more practical, especially because the envelopes have a nasty habit of falling apart. The compartments are perfect for me (and you can even remove the insert if you want to keep it VERY simple). It has two billfolds, something I always want because I travel a lot and can keep different currencies organized. The leather is soft and supple and the two-toned detail looks classy. Everything is well aligned and sewn together, and the zipper looks like it will last.

This may well be my wallet for a long time to come.

One good thing about this cuff is it softens up over time the more you wear it and becomes even more comfortable.  At the same time- the one I received did not soften up so much that the tip became floppy no matter which hole I put the pin into.  If you want to keep it supple I'd recommend storing it in the closed position- buckled up in the same hole that you wear it in most often when it's on your wrist.  If you find it doesn't fit quite as you like- but want the same look- the leather in this cuff is thick enough that you can add an extra hole or two  into it if done carefully; or you can wear this one notch looser than you usually would.  The one I got stayed stiff enough that it doesn't slide around much even if you wear it looser and do not happen to have the wrist of a body builder. (as most don't)  The cuff looks better in person than it does in the picture...the contrast between the leather and metal works well and doesn't scream LOOK AT MY WRIST THERE'S SOMETHING DIFFERENT ON MY WRIST as you might think from the picture.  Seems well made though keep In mind any leather can dry out and crack over time and adding conditioner paste to a cuff that isn't plain might not be worth the mess.  But overall if you want to bulk out your wriist or accessorize with other black items you wear this is probably a good choice cuff.  Hope this helps

I received this as a review sample and thought it would be a novelty more than a functional timepiece. I was wrong. While I still rely on my phone's clock this watch is perfect for camping, hiking and similar activities.

One of the things that I love is the fact that it has the look of an analog watch, but is brimming with digital features as well. I mention the analog part because at 66 (at the time of this review) I grew up in an era where all watches were analog and there is an imprinted relationship between the position of the hands and the time of day. I suspect many folks in my age group can 'visualize' time better that way.

Of course, the biggest draw for me is the price. If I were to break or lose this watch I am not going to have an anxiety attack. Lose it I may, but I doubt if this think will break easily. It's water and dust proof, and seems to be relatively shock proof as well.

It's a bit large, but not unduly uncomfortable to wear, especially for the short periods that I use it. Bottom line is it's accurate since it has a digital movement, is packed with features that you can read in the description, and nearly indestructible. And, of course, inexpensive.

This is a very nice, high quality wallet. You can tell a lot went into the craftsmanship and the materials are excellent. The woven finish definitely brings a level of sophistication to the piece and the stitching is flawless. The reason that I deducted 3 stars was because it suffers from a huge design flaw that no wallet of this caliber should ever suffer from. Because this is an 8 credit card wallet, it's 4 cards per side. They card slits are horizontal and so when you fill this wallet with cards, it sits closed flush and has a tendency to twist because the area of contact between to the 2 sides is too small. What this means is when you pull the wallet out of your pocket it has a disheveled look to it because it is presented as "crooked". I'll live with this flaw but I won't buy another like it. I'll be stuck with this wallet for some time and I am ok with it because it is nice, it just has a messy look because the credit cards touch each other in a staggered formation when closed. This is "teaching" the leather a dis-symmetry that I will be fighting for the rest of the wallet's life.

I am including 2 pictures to illustrate my complaint - One of a side view to show how the credit cards sit against each when closed and one of the wallet a rest to show the effect of the design.

If Montblanc or the Amazon seller wishes to rectify this I am welcome to do so and would restore my faith in these companies, however I fear they likely won't respond and I'm stuck with a fancy wallet that looks sloppy.

This is a nice cowhide belt. My husband likes his belts, so they have to his kind of style. He likes the nice looking belts that aren't like the belts everyone is wearing. He likes this belt. He likes how easy it is to adjust the belt. I can't say I have ever seen a belt like these before. I was a little confused I have to admit when I first saw it. The one end of the belt has these bumps that lock the buckle in place. The bump catch on the buckle well and doesn't move til you release it. There is a lever on the one side of the buckle to release the belt. You might have to tighten the belt slightly to release it. The belt is long and my husband has several extra inches. The belt fit nicely in his belt loops and the extra belt sits in his loops well too. The belt is also fairly flexible and not stiff. It is comfortable to wear and holds my husband's pants up well. I received this product for free for testing and reviewing purposes, and this review is based on my own personal experience using this product.

The first thing I noticed about this belt was how heavy it was.  It isn't a cheap discount store product.  I wasn't sure on the length, but it fit both of us fine.  While marketed for men, it is absolutely a unisex item.
This belt has a feature I have never seen in a belt before.  It doesn't have holes to adjust it. It is more of a zip tie contraption.  And the "zip" covers enough area that it really is a one size fits most.  It snugs down to whatever position you need it. No more poking extra holes or holes ripping through.  I have to be honest though, and "releasing" the belt had me stumped for a minute.  I couldn't figure out how to get the darn thing off!  It was simple really, there is a small lever to lift, and it releases it.

This is a very nice, albeit large, watch and pedometer. I've owned several pedometers over the past few years, and if you're used to all the bells, whistles, and customization that's available in higher-end models, you're not going to be very happy with the basic odometer in this watch. If you are just looking for a basic pedometer/watch combination that is very affordable and very well made, then this should fit the bill.

Steps are only recorded while in pedometer mode, and these are only displayed as steps. There's no conversion to distance. The reason for this is that there's no way to adjust or customize your stride length. You have to remember to turn on pedometer mode when walking or running, or your steps will not be recorded.

The watch face is approximately 1.75", the display area being just over 1 inch of that. This means you have a very large and easily readable display. There are four different buttons positioned around the watch. One just turns the light on and off (only the numbers glow, not the entire watch face.) The mode button controls pedometer mode, display mode, and allows you to take your pulse.

The remaining two buttons allow you to select options while in the various modes, as well as adjust time and so on. You can also review the memory and display how many steps were recorded. When displaying your recorded steps the watch alternates between steps, calories, and kilometers. The kilometers is only a guess, as there is no way to set your stride length.

For basic pedometer, and a full-featured watch, this is a great bargain. Especially since it is water resistant past 100'  although I have not tested that part out. Free sample provided for honest review.

I want to preface this review with... I am a bow-tie junkie. I have quite a few (50+) bow-tie within my collection. What that said...

I found this brand while searching for new colors and designs for a cruise in the Caribbean. I wanted unique colors and patterns that would work well for both formal evenings as well as normal casual dinners. I was also looking for good material that would hold the correct shape, while being easy to tie and untie as some materials are stiff or cause friction against itself. These little beauties are GREAT. They tie easily, have a wonderful look and have great color choices. Best of all they also come with pocket squares which in some cases would normally be the same price as the tie itself. Having the matching pocket square for the jacket makes all the difference in the world.

If you are looking to either have just one bow-tie for a special event, several to add to your collection for lots to build a collection I certainly recommend these as they will not break the pocketbook and will last a long long time through wear after wear.

If you have never tried a bow-tie I HIGHLY suggest it as it is such as classy statement with a nice suit, or even with a button up and jeans. They are great for most occasions and have the added bonus of not getting in the way when eating, drinking and therefore do not have the hazard of having food dripped, dropped or dragged across them.

100 years ago the fly's on men's pants were fastened with buttons.  Then the zipper changed all that.  Most belts now require a fastener into one of several holes for best fit.  The problem is that every time the belt is fastened, it needs to be flexed back and tensioned in an unnatural state.  Eventually the belt wears out because of all that crimping and tension.  This belt eliminates the holes along with regular belt fastening issues.  Fastening with this belt is very straightforward, smooth & zipper like, with even a zip like feel & sound.  Tightness is adjusted in fractions of an inch. The design appears to be quite solid, but time will tell if these belts will hold up.

This is an ingenious buckle design.  I go up and down in my waist size and this belt is great for multiple sizes.  Also, on days that I tuck a shirt into my pants, my size changes just a little and this belt keeps my pants comfortable.  I would prefer a little thicker leather (the reason I didn't give it 5 stars), but the price and quality of the belt and buckle have been great. After the quality of Hanes briefs went down so badly (the elastic cracks and loses all elesicity after only a few washings) I was on a hunt for new briefs.
Years ago, I only bought Calvin Klein briefs and found them to be the best.
Then, becoming more frugal as time went by, I tried a bunch of cheapies and I found Hanes to be the best of the low priced briefs.
THEN, Hanes cheapened the elastic SO badly that I had to throw away a batch I bought due to the elastic becoming brittle, crackiing and losing ALL elasticity while the rest of the briefs were in great shape.
Been using the SAME washing machine on regular cycle with warm water.
The SAME dryer on the "auto-sense" cycle that senses when the clothes are dry.
Both machines are Estate by Whirlpool machines that are 15 years old.
I've been using the SAME liquid Tide detergent and NEVER used bleach.
So, doing away with the variable of the machines and the detergent, I am certain that Hanes cheapened the quality of the elastic. (I still have OLD Hanes briefs where the elastic is fine)
So, the search was on. I bought the following at the same time here on Amazon:
1 package of Jockey Men's Underwear Classic Full Rise Brief - 6 Pack. I wear a Large in all other brands but since these come in waist size, I bought what I was told by Jockey which was a size 36 waist which is supposed to be the equivalent to a Large. Price - $36.00 or 6 bucks per brief
1 package of  Calvin Klein Men's Underwear Cotton Classics 4 Pack Briefs. Size Large. Price $26.95 so that's $6.74 per brief.
1 pack of Fruit of the Loom Men's Breathable Brief Assorted Colors (Pack of 4). Size Large, $12.99 so that's $3.24 per brief.
SIZE: The Jockey's were the SMALLEST, then came the Calvin Klein which are about an inch bigger and then the Fruit of the Loom which are even bigger than the Calvin Klein.
So, the smallest is the Jockey's, next is the Calvin Klein's and then the Fruit of the Loom.
The elastic is about the same quality on all three brands.
The material is about the same on all three brands.
I just washed all three packages of all three brands of brand new briefs to check the size after washing. I never wear anything right out of the package before washing.
SO,, believe it or not, I find the Fruit of the Loom to be the best of the three. ESPECIALLY for the price.
The Calvin Klein are good, but NOT as good as the Calvins I bought years ago.
The Jockey's come in last for size, quality and price.
Pleasant surprise for me that I tried the Fruit of the Loom after all these years.
Not that the Fruit of the Loom are so great, it's more that the name brands like Jockey and Calvin Klein lowered their quality but not the price.
TOTALLY forget about Hanes. What a shame that had to throw out a drawer full of Hanes that look like new  but the elastic rendered them totally useless.
I'm sticking with Fruit of the Loom. Good quality and the best bang for the buck!

Because I prefer total freedom of movement but also want to keep "the boys" snug and supported, I want underwear that covers my entire crotch and bottom but nothing else...especially not my upper/lower legs. The underwear I buy could be considered "cheap" seeing as I always tend to buy it in multi-packs of 6-8 pairs from Walmart, Target, JC Penney, etc...and I like my underwear to be classic full or mid-rise and snug WHITE BRIEFS. I'll say it...I'm 29 and I prefer "tighty whities" just like I wore as a boy.

My partner who is a couple of years younger than me and wears nothing but boxer briefs, has tried several times over the last year to get me to switch to boxer briefs but I refuse. So as a joke for my birthday a few weeks ago, he thought it would be funny to buy me underwear and socks in addition to the meaningful gift he actually got me. When it came to underwear, these FTL breathable briefs are what he gave me. I looked at the package, held it up to him and just rolled my eyes...to which he responded "just give them a try for me".  Once I put them on, I was pleasantly surprised at how comfortable and supportive they are. I love the light, airy fabric and the fact that they fit just like the regular white FTL briefs I've worn for years. The waistband is actually wider and softer than other briefs I own, so that is another positive about them, and I actually don't look half bad wearing them (or at least my partner thinks so).

The only issue I have with them is that FTL does not sell them in plain/solid white. I'm not sure why, but I want classic uniformity and simplicity when it comes to my underwear, and "tighty whities" (or whatever people call them) are what gives me that. I will still wear these simply because they are comfortable, but PLEASE PLEASE start selling these breathable briefs in solid white with the same thick waistband and cooling fabric.

I ordered the "Coral," which is a bit of a misnomer, because it doesn't look like coral to me at all. This review is for the green tie.

This is a gorgeous tie.  I plan on keeping it, but I will not buy any more ties from this company.  Why?  The packaging leaves a firm crease that is a bit of a pain to remove.  Why would a company that primarily sells ties package a tie in such a stupid way as to leave a very firm crease where it will be visible when worn?!?

The tie arrives in a black envelope, approximately 15" long. When I first saw the package, I thought it looked rather nice.  Then I removed the tie and saw a very prominent crease.  I have a short torso, but when tied, the crease is below the knot and very visible.  It can be removed with an iron on silk setting and a soft cloth to cover the tie with.  But I would not order a tie knowing that I would have to spend time ironing it to make it wearable.  I have ordered a number of ties online, and this is the first time I have ever received one with any crease, yet alone one so prominent and in a spot that would be visible when worn.

Because of the way the tie is folded to fit in the envelope, there are actually two creases, one on the thicker front-facing part, and one on the thinner part that is hidden when the tie is worn.  The latter is not such a big deal, but the former is just absurd.

Other ties I have purchased online are folded about halfway, so that the crease will not be visible when tied, and then loosely folded so as not to cause additional creases.  That is how it should be done.

Again, that being said, this is an absolutely gorgeous tie.  The green is more of a turquoise/teal color, and it really pops in real life, but the pattern is subtle enough to keep the tie from being too loud.  It's very vibrant, but at the same time not too distracting.  I would highly recommend it if the company fixed their packaging, or if you do not care about having to iron out a crease on a newly purchased tie.

THEN, Hanes cheapened the elastic SO badly that I had to throw away a batch I bought due to the elastic becoming brittle, crackiing and losing ALL elasticity while the rest of the briefs were in great shape.

The SAME dryer on the "auto-sense" cycle that senses when the clothes are dry.
Both machines are Estate by Whirlpool machines that are 15 years old.
I've been using the SAME liquid Tide detergent and NEVER used bleach.
So, doing away with the variable of the machines and the detergent, I am certain that Hanes cheapened the quality of the elastic. (I still have OLD Hanes briefs where the elastic is fine)
So, the search was on. I bought the following at the same time here on Amazon:
1 package of Jockey Men's Underwear Classic Full Rise Brief - 6 Pack. I wear a Large in all other brands but since these come in waist size, I bought what I was told by Jockey which was a size 36 waist which is supposed to be the equivalent to a Large. Price - $36.00 or 6 bucks per brief
1 package of  Calvin Klein Men's Underwear Cotton Classics 4 Pack Briefs. Size Large. Price $26.95 so that's $6.74 per brief.
1 pack of Fruit of the Loom Men's Breathable Brief Assorted Colors (Pack of 4). Size Large, $12.99 so that's $3.24 per brief.
SIZE: The Jockey's were the SMALLEST, then came the Calvin Klein which are about an inch bigger and then the Fruit of the Loom which are even bigger than the Calvin Klein.

The elastic is about the same quality on all three brands.
The material is about the same on all three brands.
I just washed all three packages of all three brands of brand new briefs to check the size after washing. I never wear anything right out of the package before washing.
SO,, believe it or not, I find the Fruit of the Loom to be the best of the three. ESPECIALLY for the price.
